listening.translation: 本次讲座的主要话题是什么？
listening.transcript: Listen to a talk in an architecture class. The Eastgate Centre in Harare, Zimbabwe, is a mixed-use complex combining retail spaces and offices. When the architect Mick Pearce was asked to design the building in the early 1990s, he faced a big challenge: how to keep all its shops and offices cool without traditional air conditioning, and do it during an economic crisis. Energy costs were high, and importing advanced air conditioners was impossible. To solve this dilemma, Pearce looked to termite mounds. Termites are insects that live in large colonies. They build big mounds on the ground throughout the African savanna. The mounds are amazing structures. Some rise three meters above ground and extend another one to three meters below the ground. The underground chambers connect to the above-ground chimneys through a maze of tunnels. And this entire system works as natural climate control. Warm air rises and escapes through the top, while cooler air flows in from below. The thick walls of soil and clay absorb heat during the day and release it at night. Termites fine-tune airflow by opening and closing vents, adding or removing soil to enlarge or seal passages. On hot days, they open more vents for cooling. listening.transcript: Listen to a talk on a biology podcast. Picture a creature that is smaller than a mouse, yet as territorial as a lion. It is the Scarlet badis, a freshwater fish about 2 centimeters long. In the wild, it thrives peacefully in slow moving streams of India. Because of its size and attractive coloring, it is popular for aquariums. However, in aquariums, males are more aggressive. They chase and nip at other males if they enter their territory, so it is crucial to include lots of vegetation. Plants act as hiding places and borderlines between male territories. Male Scarlet badis are vivid orangish red with light bluish stripes. When a male is not in a confrontation, his scarlet is less bright and can almost resemble the dull gray female coloring. If you can see any scarlet at all, it is a male. Males are usually a bit larger than females. During breeding season, males show their brightest coloring and do a dance to impress females.

speaking.answer: I think it can go both ways, but for me it's mostly helpful. When I want to meet a friend, I just send a quick message, and we can decide on a time in two minutes. Last week we planned a whole dinner in one group chat. Um, that's so much easier than calling everyone one by one. Social media also shows me what my friends are doing, so I know when someone is free or visiting my city. Of course, there are times when people sit together at a table and stare at their phones, and that's honestly sad. But I don't blame the apps, I blame the habits. So overall, I believe social media makes face-to-face meetings more likely, as long as people put their phones away once they're together. A simple rule like phones in the middle of the table works well for my group.

Make a contribution to the discussion in your own words. An effective response will contain at least 100 words. Today we will discuss the role of technology in modern education. As you know, technology can enhance learning by providing access to a wealth of information and interactive tools. However, many people believe that technology can be a distraction and hinder traditional learning methods. So, technology can be beneficial or harmful to learners depending on the context. But considered in general terms, has technology had a positive or negative effect on modern education as a whole? Explain your reasoning.
content.post: Paul: Overreliance on technology prevents learners from developing critical thinking skills and solving problems independently. A well-rounded education is only possible through traditional teaching and learning methods.

writing.answer:
Overall, technology has had a positive effect on education because it expands access to instruction and makes practice more adaptable. Claire is right that students can use libraries, simulations, and feedback to study concepts that may be difficult to visualize. A rural student, for example, can take an advanced course that the school cannot offer.

Paul's concern about overreliance is valid. Copying quick online answers can weaken independent reasoning, and constant notifications interrupt concentration. These are problems of instructional design, not proof that technology itself is harmful. Teachers can require students to explain their reasoning, evaluate competing sources, and complete some discussions or calculations without devices.

Technology is most valuable when it extends a capable teacher rather than replacing one. Schools should combine online resources with direct feedback, collaborative work, experiments, and sustained reading. Used under clear rules, digital tools give more students access to expertise and repeated practice while traditional methods continue to develop judgment, patience, and human communication.

reading.title: Human Brain Function
reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
reading.passage: The human brain is an extraordinarily intricate organ, unrivaled in its complexity and function. Studying its anatomy reveals a remarkable internal architecture, composed of billions of neurons intricately interconnected by synapses. These neurons [1] tran____ electrical [2] impu____, facilitating [3] t__ brain's [4] ro__ in [5] enab____ cognition, [6] proce_____ information, [7] regul_____ essential [8] bod___ functions, [9] a__ facilitating [10] emot____. The reflective nature of studying the brain encourages careful consideration of how its structure impacts behavior and thought.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: The human brain is an extraordinarily intricate organ, unrivaled in its complexity and function. Studying its anatomy reveals a remarkable internal architecture, composed of billions of neurons intricately interconnected by synapses. These neurons [1] tran____ electrical [2] impu____, facilitating [3] t__ brain's [4] ro__ in [5] enab____ cognition, [6] proce_____ information, [7] regul_____ essential [8] bod___ functions, [9] a__ facilitating [10] emot____. The reflective nature of studying the brain encourages careful consideration of how its structure impacts behavior and thought.

reading.answer:
1. smit → transmit
2. lses → impulses
3. he → the
4. le → role
5. ling → enabling
6. ssing → processing
7. ating → regulating
8. ily → bodily
9. nd → and
10. ions → emotions
reading.explanation: 1. transmit 意为传输，与上下文“神经元传输电脉冲”一致；前缀 tran- 表示横穿或传输，符合 electrical impulses 的搭配。 2. impulses 意为脉冲，常与 electrical 搭配表示电脉冲；impu- 是词根，表示推动，与神经元传递信息相关。 3. the 是定冠词，用于特指大脑的角色；在 facilitating t__ brain's role 中，t 后填 he 组成 the，表示特指。 4. role 意为角色，与 brain's 搭配表示大脑的功能或作用；ro- 后填 le 组成 role，在语境中指大脑在认知等方面的角色。 5. enabling 意为使能够，enab- 后填 ling 组成 enabling；in enabling cognition 表示在使认知成为可能方面。 6. processing 意为处理，与 information 搭配表示信息处理；proce- 后填 ssing 组成 processing，与前文 cognition 并列。 7. regulating 意为调节，regul- 后填 ating 组成 regulating；与 essential bodily functions 搭配，表示调节身体功能。 8. bodily 意为身体的，bod- 后填 ily 组成 bodily；修饰 functions，表示身体功能。 9. and 是并列连词，用于连接 facilitating emotions 和前面的列表；a 后填 nd 组成 and，表示并列关系。 10. emotions 意为情绪，emot- 后填 ions 组成 emotions；与 facilitating 搭配，表示促进情绪，与前文 cognition 等并列。
reading.translation: 人脑是极其复杂的器官，在复杂性与功能上无可匹敌。研究其解剖揭示非凡的内部架构，由通过突触精密互联的数十亿神经元组成。这些神经元传递电脉冲，促成大脑在启用认知、处理信息、调节基本身体功能与促进情绪方面的作用。研究大脑的反思性鼓励仔细考虑其结构如何影响行为与思想。

Although the Crusades were primarily military campaigns, they [1] facil______ contact [2] th__ led [3] t_ the [4] tran____ of [5] id___ and [6] techno____. European [7] scho____ gained [8] acc___ to [9] adva____ knowledge [10] i_ mathematics and medicine from the Islamic world, sparking renewed intellectual activity. Translations of Arabic philosophical texts, including commentaries on Aristotle, challenged existing doctrines and inspired new schools of thought. content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: The cultural exchange between Europe and the Near East during the medieval period had a lasting impact on art, science, and philosophy. Although the Crusades were primarily military campaigns, they [1] facil______ contact [2] th__ led [3] t_ the [4] tran____ of [5] id___ and [6] techno____. European [7] scho____ gained [8] acc___ to [9] adva____ knowledge [10] i_ mathematics and medicine from the Islamic world, sparking renewed intellectual activity. Translations of Arabic philosophical texts, including commentaries on Aristotle, challenged existing doctrines and inspired new schools of thought. This exchange helped reshape European intellectual life.

reading.answer:
1. itated → facilitated
2. at → that
3. o → to
4. sfer → transfer
5. eas → ideas
6. logy → technology
7. lars → scholars
8. ess → access
9. nced → advanced
10. n → in
reading.explanation: 1. facilitated是动词facilitate的过去式，意为“促进”，描述十字军行动如何促成接触。 2. that引导定语从句，修饰前面的contact，表示这个接触导致了后续的影响。 3. to与led组成固定短语led to，意为“导致”，后面接名词transfer。 4. transfer是名词，意为“转移”，指思想和技术的传递过程。 5. ideas是复数名词，与technology并列，指思想内容。 6. technology是单数名词，与ideas并列，指技术知识。 7. scholars是复数名词，指欧洲的学者群体，他们获得了知识。 8. access与gained和to搭配成gained access to，表示获得利用知识的机会。 9. advanced是形容词，修饰knowledge，表示先进的或高级的知识。 10. in是介词，用于指出知识的具体领域，如数学和医学。
reading.translation: 中世纪欧洲与近东之间的文化交流对艺术、科学与哲学有持久影响。尽管十字军东征主要是军事行动，它们促进了导致思想与技术转移的接触。欧洲学者从伊斯兰世界获得数学与医学的先进知识，激发新的智识活动。阿拉伯哲学文本——包括对亚里士多德的注释——的翻译挑战了既有教义并启发新思想流派。这一交流帮助重塑欧洲智识生活。

reading.title: The Academic Benefits of Arts Education
reading.prompt: The word "foster" in the passage is closest in meaning to
reading.promptZh: 文中单词“foster”的含义最接近：
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Several recent studies suggest that children's participation in arts programs, whether visual arts, music, drama, or dance, can foster cognitive development. Empirical studies have highlighted positive correlations between arts engagement and improvements in reading, mathematics, language development, and social skills. Similarly, comprehensive analyses emphasize that arts education contributes to both cognitive and emotional growth, which in turn supports academic success.

Paragraph 2
Broader educational reports reinforce these findings. Schools that integrate the arts into their core curricula often document more positive learning environments. When children collaborate in theater, music ensembles, or group visual arts projects, they build a sense of belonging and shared purpose—key components of motivation and engagement, factors known to influence academic achievement.

Paragraph 3
Though persuasive, the evidence is not uniformly conclusive. Some studies rely on correlational data—meaning that they demonstrate that arts program participation is related to academic success without proving that arts programs cause academic success. Researchers also note that the benefits of arts education often depend on factors such as teacher expertise and skillful integration of the arts with broader learning goals. And, in some cases, arts programs are too brief or inconsistently delivered to produce measurable academic effects, which may partly explain mixed findings in the literature.

reading.translation:
文中单词“foster”的含义最接近：

若干近期研究表明，儿童参与艺术项目——无论视觉艺术、音乐、戏剧还是舞蹈——都能促进认知发展。实证研究强调艺术参与与阅读、数学、语言发展及社交技能提升之间的正相关。同样，综合分析指出艺术教育有助于认知与情感成长，进而支持学业成功。
更广泛的教育报告也强化了这些发现。把艺术融入核心课程的学校往往记录到更积极的学习环境。当儿童在戏剧、音乐合奏或集体视觉艺术项目中协作时，他们会建立起归属感与共同目标——这些是动机与投入的关键组成部分，也是已知会影响学业成就的因素。
尽管有说服力，证据并非一律确凿。有些研究依赖相关数据——即它们表明参与艺术项目与学业成功相关，但并未证明艺术项目导致学业成功。研究者还指出，艺术教育的益处往往取决于教师专业能力以及艺术与更广泛学习目标的巧妙融合等因素。此外，有些艺术项目时间过短或实施不一致，难以产生可测量的学业效果，这可能部分解释文献中的结果不一。

reading.title: The Academic Benefits of Arts Education
reading.prompt: The passage mentions each of the following about children who participate in arts programs EXCEPT:
reading.promptZh: 文章提到参与艺术项目的儿童具有以下特点，除了：
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Several recent studies suggest that children's participation in arts programs, whether visual arts, music, drama, or dance, can foster cognitive development. Empirical studies have highlighted positive correlations between arts engagement and improvements in reading, mathematics, language development, and social skills. Similarly, comprehensive analyses emphasize that arts education contributes to both cognitive and emotional growth, which in turn supports academic success.

Paragraph 2
Broader educational reports reinforce these findings. Schools that integrate the arts into their core curricula often document more positive learning environments. When children collaborate in theater, music ensembles, or group visual arts projects, they build a sense of belonging and shared purpose—key components of motivation and engagement, factors known to influence academic achievement.

Paragraph 3
Though persuasive, the evidence is not uniformly conclusive. Some studies rely on correlational data—meaning that they demonstrate that arts program participation is related to academic success without proving that arts programs cause academic success. Researchers also note that the benefits of arts education often depend on factors such as teacher expertise and skillful integration of the arts with broader learning goals. And, in some cases, arts programs are too brief or inconsistently delivered to produce measurable academic effects, which may partly explain mixed findings in the literature.

reading.answer:
1. orative → collaborative
2. f → of
3. ters → fosters
4. amic → dynamic
5. ong → among
6. at → that
7. ivity → creativity
8. an → can
9. ceived → preconceived
10. nd → and
reading.explanation: 1. collab 后需填 orative 组成 collaborative，意为“合作的”，指剧院的合作性质，与后文 dynamic exchange 相呼应。 2. o 后需填 f 组成 of，用于固定搭配 nature of theater，表示“剧院的性质”，使短语完整。 3. fos 后需填 ters 组成 fosters，意为“促进”，指剧院培养专业人士间的动态交流。 4. dyn 后需填 amic 组成 dynamic，意为“动态的”，形容交流的活跃和变化特性。 5. am 后需填 ong 组成 among，意为“在……之间”，表示交流发生在专业人士中。 6. th 后需填 at 组成 that，引导定语从句修饰 exchange，指这种交流激发创造力。 7. creat 后需填 ivity 组成 creativity，意为“创造力”，指剧院促进创新思维。 8. c 后需填 an 组成 can，表示能力，指剧院能够挑战先入为主的观念。 9. precon 后需填 ceived 组成 preconceived，意为“先入为主的”，修饰 notions，指固有观念。 10. a 后需填 nd 组成 and，连接 challenge 和 invite，表示并列动作，邀请观众考虑不同视角。
reading.translation: 与文学或视觉艺术不同，戏剧通过现场表演吸引观众，创造即时情感连接。戏剧的协作性质促进专业人士之间动态交流，激发创意。戏剧可挑战先入之见，并邀请观众考虑多元视角。其短暂性——仅存在于表演瞬间——强化影响，迫使表演者与观者都投入当下，最终改变其对人类体验的理解。

reading.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Challenges
reading.prompt: Why does the author mention the “indiscriminate use of antibiotics”?
reading.promptZh: 作者提及“抗生素的滥用”是为了什么？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR)—the ability of microorganisms to withstand drugs that once killed them—threatens to reverse decades of medical advancement, posing an urgent public health challenge globally. In particular, the widespread and often indiscriminate use of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture has accelerated the emergence of resistant bacteria. Recognizing the gravity of AMR, the World Health Organization classifies it among the top global health threats, underscoring the critical need for immediate action.

Paragraph 2
Bacteria develop resistance through a multitude of mechanisms, including genetic mutations and the sharing of genes, which allow them to survive antibiotic treatment and proliferate. Unfortunately, the pharmaceutical industry has been slow to produce new antibiotics, hampered by both scientific obstacles and economic disincentives. Antibiotics often yield lower financial returns compared to medications for chronic diseases. Therefore, they receive less investment.

Paragraph 3
Addressing AMR requires a comprehensive and coordinated international strategy. Implementing stringent regulations on antibiotic prescriptions can curb misuse but might not eliminate it completely. Financial incentives for pharmaceutical companies could stimulate the development of novel antibiotics. However, this approach remains contentious due to the varying perspectives on economic feasibility. Public health campaigns aimed at educating communities about judicious antibiotic use are vital, but experts continue to debate the most effective strategy.

reading.translation:
作者提及“抗生素的滥用”是为了什么？

抗菌药耐药（AMR）——微生物抵抗曾能杀死它们的药物的能力——威胁逆转数十年医学进步，构成全球紧迫的公共卫生挑战。尤其是医学与农业中广泛且往往无差别地使用抗生素，加速了耐药细菌的出现。认识到 AMR 的严重性，世界卫生组织将其列为全球首要健康威胁之一，强调立即行动的关键必要。
细菌通过多种机制发展耐药，包括基因突变与基因共享，使其在抗生素治疗中存活并增殖。不幸的是，制药业生产新抗生素进展缓慢，既受科学障碍也受经济负激励拖累。与慢性病药物相比，抗生素财务回报往往更低，因此获得的投资更少。
应对 AMR 需要全面协调的国际策略。对抗生素处方实施严格监管可抑制滥用，却未必能完全消除。对制药公司的财务激励可刺激新型抗生素研发，但因对经济可行性的观点不一，这一做法仍有争议。旨在教育社区合理使用抗生素的公共卫生宣传至关重要，但专家仍在争论最有效的策略。

reading.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Challenges
reading.prompt: The passage mentions each of the following strategies for addressing antimicrobial resistance EXCEPT
reading.promptZh: 文章提及了以下应对抗生素耐药性的策略，除了
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR)—the ability of microorganisms to withstand drugs that once killed them—threatens to reverse decades of medical advancement, posing an urgent public health challenge globally. In particular, the widespread and often indiscriminate use of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture has accelerated the emergence of resistant bacteria. Recognizing the gravity of AMR, the World Health Organization classifies it among the top global health threats, underscoring the critical need for immediate action.

Paragraph 2
Bacteria develop resistance through a multitude of mechanisms, including genetic mutations and the sharing of genes, which allow them to survive antibiotic treatment and proliferate. Unfortunately, the pharmaceutical industry has been slow to produce new antibiotics, hampered by both scientific obstacles and economic disincentives. Antibiotics often yield lower financial returns compared to medications for chronic diseases. Therefore, they receive less investment.

Paragraph 3
Addressing AMR requires a comprehensive and coordinated international strategy. Implementing stringent regulations on antibiotic prescriptions can curb misuse but might not eliminate it completely. Financial incentives for pharmaceutical companies could stimulate the development of novel antibiotics. However, this approach remains contentious due to the varying perspectives on economic feasibility. Public health campaigns aimed at educating communities about judicious antibiotic use are vital, but experts continue to debate the most effective strategy.

listening.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Woman: You just started working at the bookstore, right? How's that going?
Man: It's okay. I like how it's close to my apartment. I can ride my bike there. I've mostly been processing orders and stocking the shelves. I just wish there was more variety. I'm doing the same tasks over and over again.
Woman: I see. Well, you could look for other jobs on campus, couldn't you?
Man: Yes, but... well, my sister is the one who got me this job. She is friends with the owner, and I would feel bad quitting after working there for such a short time.

女：明白。可以找校内别的工作吧？
男：可以，不过……这份工作是姐姐介绍的。她跟老板是朋友，干这么短就辞我会过意不去。

listening.transcript:
Listen to part of a talk in a psychology class.
Imagine you're a painter. Now, would your passion for painting be driven purely by internal motivation? In other words, would you paint just for the joy of it? What if you're being paid for your paintings? Intuitively, we might assume that an external reward or financial incentive would amplify your motivation. But that's not the case. Paradoxically, the opposite often occurs, a phenomenon known in psychology as the overjustification effect. Intrinsic motivation decreases when external incentives come into play. Let me describe an experiment from the 1970s. Children who naturally gravitated toward drawing with markers were observed. Some children were promised rewards for their drawings. Then, during free time, the group that expected rewards spent significantly less time drawing compared to other kids, suggesting that extrinsic rewards can lower an individual's interest. The underlying mechanism here is a perceived shift in autonomy. So, take an activity that's initially pursued just for the fun of it. Introduce an external reward, and individuals feel their actions are no longer self-driven, but driven by the reward itself. The activity feels more like an obligation than a passion. And you can imagine implications across various fields: education, business...
where encouraging intrinsic motivation is crucial. Students or employees who are rewarded for activities they already enjoy could lose their natural enthusiasm over time. Understanding the overjustification effect can help us when we're creating settings intended to nurture, not suppress, intrinsic motivation.

想象你是画家。你对绘画的热情会纯由内在动机驱动吗？换句话说，你会只为乐趣而画吗？若画作出售拿报酬呢？直觉上我们可能假定外部奖励或金钱激励会放大动机。但并非如此。矛盾的是，常出现相反情况——心理学中称为过度合理化效应的现象。外部激励介入时，内在动机下降。我描述一九七〇年代的一项实验。观察了自然喜欢用水彩笔画画的儿童。有些儿童被许诺画作有奖。随后在自由时间，预期有奖的那组画画时间明显少于其他孩子，表明外部奖励可降低个人兴趣。背后机制是自主感的感知转变。所以，拿一项起初只为好玩而做的活动。引入外部奖励，个体会感到行动不再由自我驱动，而由奖励本身驱动。活动更像义务而非热情。你可以想象跨多领域的含义：教育、商业……在这些领域鼓励内在动机至关重要。因已享受的活动而受奖的学生或员工，久而久之可能失去天然热情。理解过度合理化效应，有助我们在设计旨在培育而非压制内在动机的环境时做得更好。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a physics podcast.
Have you ever wondered why ice floats on water? It's a curious phenomenon that has puzzled scientists for centuries. Normally, solids are denser than liquids because their molecules are packed more closely together. But water has a unique molecular structure and it behaves differently. As water molecules cool and form ice, they arrange themselves in a crystalline structure that occupies more space than when they are in liquid form. This arrangement causes ice to be less dense than liquid water, enabling it to float. But why is this important beyond just curiosity? Well, imagine a world where ice sank. Lakes and ponds would freeze from the bottom up, and this could have a huge impact on aquatic ecosystems. Aquatic life relies on ice forming at the surface, which creates an insulating layer that prevents the entire body of water from freezing. This insulation is vital for the survival of fish and other animals during harsh winters. Even if the top layer is frozen, they can survive in the water underneath. Floating ice, especially in polar regions, also reflects a significant amount of sunlight back into space. This helps regulate global temperatures. If ice sank, it wouldn't remain on the surface to reflect sunlight. It'd disappear beneath the water, allowing more solar energy to be absorbed by the darker ocean or lake surfaces. This would lead to warmer water temperatures, accelerating global warming and disrupting climate patterns worldwide.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段物理播客的讲座。
你是否想过为何冰浮在水上？这是困扰科学家数世纪的奇特现象。通常固体比液体密度大，因为分子堆得更紧。但水有独特分子结构，表现不同。当水分子冷却并形成冰时，它们排列成比液态时占据更多空间的晶体结构。这种排列使冰密度小于液态水，从而能浮起。但除了好奇之外这为何重要？想象一个冰会下沉的世界。湖泊与池塘会从底部向上结冰，这可能对水生生态系统产生巨大影响。水生生命依赖冰在表面形成，从而创造防止整片水体结冰的绝缘层。这种绝缘对鱼和其他动物在严冬中存活至关重要。即便表层结冰，它们仍可在下方水中存活。浮冰，尤其在极地，也把大量阳光反射回太空。这有助调节全球温度。若冰下沉，它不会留在表面反射阳光。它会消失在水下，让更多太阳能被较暗的海洋或湖面吸收。这将导致水温升高，加速全球变暖并扰乱全球气候模式。

listening.translation: 这段讲座的主要话题是什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a psychology class.

Man: Positive reinforcement is a powerful concept in psychology and behavior training. It means giving a reward after someone performs an action you want them to do again. The basic idea is that when a behavior leads to a positive outcome, it's more likely to be repeated. In other words, we tend to repeat actions that bring us something positive. This principle applies to both humans and animals, but the way it works can differ. Animals need to receive rewards immediately after the desired behavior. For example, if a dog sits and gets a treat right away, it learns that sitting leads to something good. If the reward comes too late, the connection is lost. Humans, however, can understand delayed rewards. They might work hard today because they're aiming for a future goal, like earning a degree. Or they might feel motivated by praise even if the reward isn't tangible or instant. But rewards must be used carefully. If a parent gives a child candy to stop whining, the child may learn that whining gets rewarded. It's like watering weeds instead of flowers. You're encouraging the wrong behavior. And if rewards are given too frequently, they can reduce a person's internal motivation, making them rely more on external incentives to take action. So while positive reinforcement is effective, it works best when applied thoughtfully and with clear intent.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段心理学课的讲座。

男：正强化是心理学与行为训练中有力的概念。意思是在某人做出你希望他再做的动作之后给予奖励。基本想法是：行为带来积极结果时，更可能被重复。换句话说，我们倾向重复能带来积极事物的动作。这一原则适用于人类与动物，但作用方式可能不同。动物需要在目标行为后立刻得到奖励。例如狗坐下马上得到零食，就学会坐下带来好事。奖励太晚会失去联结。人类却能理解延迟奖励。他们可能今天努力是为了未来目标，比如拿学位。也可能被表扬激励，即便奖励不具体或不即时。但奖励必须谨慎使用。若父母给孩子糖果让其停止哭闹，孩子可能学会哭闹会得奖。就像给杂草浇水而不是花。你在鼓励错误行为。奖励给得太频繁，还会削弱内在动机，使人更依赖外部激励才行动。因此正强化虽有效，最好经深思熟虑、意图明确地使用。

listening.translation: 演讲者关于动物训练提出了什么观点？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a psychology class.

Man: Positive reinforcement is a powerful concept in psychology and behavior training. It means giving a reward after someone performs an action you want them to do again. The basic idea is that when a behavior leads to a positive outcome, it's more likely to be repeated. In other words, we tend to repeat actions that bring us something positive. This principle applies to both humans and animals, but the way it works can differ. Animals need to receive rewards immediately after the desired behavior. For example, if a dog sits and gets a treat right away, it learns that sitting leads to something good. If the reward comes too late, the connection is lost. Humans, however, can understand delayed rewards. They might work hard today because they're aiming for a future goal, like earning a degree. Or they might feel motivated by praise even if the reward isn't tangible or instant. But rewards must be used carefully. If a parent gives a child candy to stop whining, the child may learn that whining gets rewarded. It's like watering weeds instead of flowers. You're encouraging the wrong behavior. And if rewards are given too frequently, they can reduce a person's internal motivation, making them rely more on external incentives to take action. So while positive reinforcement is effective, it works best when applied thoughtfully and with clear intent.

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a health podcast.

Woman: Today we're going to talk about the importance of sleep for cognitive function. Sleep is crucial for maintaining various aspects of brain health. One of the key benefits of sleep is the consolidation of memory. During sleep, particularly during the deep sleep stages, the brain processes and stores information acquired during the day, making it easier to recall later. During deep sleep, the brain also undergoes a process that flushes out neurotoxins like beta amyloid, which are linked to Alzheimer's disease. Sleep helps in learning new skills and knowledge by strengthening neural connections, and it allows the brain to enhance problem solving abilities by reorganizing information. Studies have shown that sleep deprivation affects cognitive functions like attention and decision making. Another crucial aspect of sleep is its role in emotional regulation. During sleep, the brain can process emotional experiences, which helps maintain emotional stability. REM sleep in particular plays a key role in recalibrating the brain's emotional circuits, helping people better manage fear and anxiety responses. People who do not get enough sleep are more likely to experience mood swings, anxiety, and depression. Despite the clear benefits of sleep, many people still struggle with getting enough rest. It's essential to prioritize sleep and adopt good sleep hygiene practices such as maintaining a regular sleep schedule, avoiding caffeine and electronic screens before bedtime, and creating a comfortable sleep environment. By doing so, individuals can improve their cognitive function and overall well being.

speaking.answer: I enjoy music the most, especially soft pop and acoustic songs, the kind you can listen to while studying or walking. Uh, I mostly experience it through appreciation, since I spend hours every day with headphones on. I have playlists for different moods, like one for running and another for rainy days. But I'm also trying to move toward creation, because I've been working out a few simple songs on my guitar. Honestly, making music yourself feels very different from listening. You understand the songs much better when you have to figure out every note. I also like visiting small art museums sometimes, but music is definitely my main love, and it's the thing I can't imagine my daily life without.

content.promptText: If you were creating art or music, would you prefer sharing your work publicly or keeping it private? What influences your decision?

speaking.answer: Hmm, I think I'd start by keeping it private and then slowly share it. When you're a beginner, you worry a lot about what other people think, and negative comments can really hurt your motivation. So at first I'd only show my work to a few close friends who I trust. Then, as I got better and felt more confident, I'd probably post it online, because feedback can help you improve. I mean, art is also meant to be shared, right? It's kind of lonely if nobody ever sees it. What influences my decision most is how confident I feel and whether the people around me are supportive. So private first, public later, that feels like the most comfortable path for me.

content.promptText: Some people think art and music can be powerful ways to communicate emotions and ideas that are difficult to express with words. Do you agree or disagree? Why?

speaking.answer: I agree that art and music can communicate emotions and ideas that words can't express easily. Sometimes a song can capture sadness or hope before a person even knows how to explain those feelings. Hmm, that's why people listen to music after breakups, before competitions, or during important memories. Visual art can do something similar by showing tension, beauty, or confusion without giving a direct statement. I mean, words are powerful, but they can also feel too exact. Art leaves space for people to connect with their own experiences, and that makes the message feel personal without feeling that the answer is fixed forever. That's why it feels powerful.

content.post: Kelly: Policy reform and corporate accountability are more effective for addressing climate change at scale. Governments can enforce emissions limits, invest in renewable energy, and regulate industries. Corporations control vast resources and supply chains, so their sustainability efforts have global impact. While individual actions matter, systemic change is necessary to meet climate goals.

writing.answer:
I believe systemic change through government policy and corporate accountability is the most effective way to combat climate change. Individual actions are meaningful because they show personal responsibility, but the scale of climate change is too large for private choices alone. Major emissions come from energy systems, transportation networks, factories, and supply chains, which individuals cannot redesign by themselves.

Paul is right that personal habits can influence culture and consumer demand. Still, those habits are much more effective when supported by strong policies. For example, people can choose public transportation only if governments invest in reliable buses and trains. Similarly, consumers can buy cleaner products only if companies are required or encouraged to produce them. Therefore, individual behavior matters, but government and corporate action creates the conditions that allow millions of people to reduce emissions together in a realistic and lasting way.

reading.explanation: 1. “Temperature difference”是固定搭配，指温度差异，且此处需要名词与后文“is caused by”构成被动语态。 2. “is caused by”是被动语态结构，表示“由……引起”，caused的过去分词形式在此处作表语。 3. “the abundance”中定冠词“the”特指后文提到的“热吸收表面”的丰富性，表示“这种丰富性”。 4. “abundance of”是固定介词搭配，表示“……的丰富性”，of引出具体事物。 5. “heat-absorbing surfaces”指热吸收表面，surfaces为复数名词，与“concrete”等例子一致。 6. “like concrete”举例说明热吸收表面的具体材料，concrete是符合语境的建筑材料名词。 7. “which retain heat”中which引导定语从句，retian与后文“release”并列，表示“保持热量”。 8. “during the day”是时间状语，表示“在白天期间”，与后文“at night”形成对比。 9. “the day”与后文“at night”对应，构成“白天吸收、夜间释放”的完整时间逻辑。 10. “and release”与“retain”并列，用and连接两个相反动作，表示“并释放它”。
reading.translation: 城市热岛（UHI）效应是城市地区温度显著高于周边农村地区的现象。这一温差由混凝土等大量吸热表面造成，它们白天蓄热并在夜间缓慢释放。城市植被减少与气流受限进一步加剧该效应，导致能耗增加、空气污染上升与健康风险——尤其在热浪期间。城市绿色空间在对抗 UHI 效应中起关键作用。

[5] Engi_____ are [6] ab__ to [7] fabr_____ lightweight, [8] str___ components [9] wi__ internal [10] struc_____ that are impossible to produce using traditional methods. content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: The advancement of 3D printing technology has revolutionized manufacturing by enabling precise, layer-by-layer fabrication of complex objects. 3D printing can use [1] div____ materials [2] su__ as [3] plas____, metals, [4] a__ ceramics. [5] Engi_____ are [6] ab__ to [7] fabr_____ lightweight, [8] str___ components [9] wi__ internal [10] struc_____ that are impossible to produce using traditional methods. In the medical field, 3D printing facilitates the production of patient-specific implants and prosthetics tailored to anatomical data from imaging scans. 3D printing enhances design flexibility and production efficiency by streamlining prototyping and reducing material waste.

reading.answer:
1. erse → diverse
2. ch → such
3. tics → plastics
4. nd → and
5. neers → Engineers
6. le → able
7. icate → fabricate
8. ong → strong
9. th → with
10. tures → structures
reading.explanation: 1. 这里需要形容词修饰materials，'diverse'表示多样的，与后文列举的塑料、金属等材料呼应。 2. 'such as'是固定短语，用于举例，后文具体列出plastics、metals和ceramics。 3. 这里需要名词复数形式，与后文的metals和ceramics并列，表示一种可3D打印的材料。 4. 在列举最后一个元素前，使用'and'连接，表示plastics、metals和ceramics三者并列。 5. 这里需要名词作句子主语，'Engineers'指工程师，后文描述他们能够制造组件。 6. 'are able to'是固定结构，表示有能力做某事，后接动词fabricate描述工程师的技能。 7. 在'able to'后需要动词原形，'fabricate'意思是制造，符合语境制造轻质坚固的组件。 8. 这里需要形容词与lightweight并列，'strong'表示坚固的，共同描述组件的特性。 9. 'with'是介词，表示具有或带有，后接internal structures描述组件包含内部结构。 10. 这里需要名词复数形式，'structures'指结构，与internal搭配，表示传统方法无法生产的内部结构。
reading.translation: 3D 打印技术的进步通过实现复杂物体的精确逐层制造革新了制造业。3D 打印可使用塑料、金属与陶瓷等多样材料。工程师能制造具有传统方法无法生产的内部结构的轻质高强度组件。在医疗领域，3D 打印促进基于影像扫描解剖数据的患者专用植入物与假肢生产。3D 打印通过简化原型制作并减少材料浪费，增强设计灵活性与生产效率。

reading.passage:
Momentum Meet-up: Networking Mixer for Students
Build real-world connections with peers, alumni, and local employers at our campus-wide mixer!
Join us on Tuesday, April 14, 5:00–7:00 P.M. in the Student Center Ballroom.
The evening features fast-paced speed-networking rounds, a short alumni insights panel, and open mingling—perfect for practicing introductions and discovering internships.
• Arrive at 4:45 P.M. for a quick networking primer led by Career Services.
• Be prepared to share five to ten copies of your résumé.
• Smart casual attire is encouraged.
• Light refreshments provided.
• Name tags and conversation starters will be provided at check-in.
• All majors and class years welcome, including graduate students.
Hosted by Career Services and Student Government, Momentum Meet-up is a friendly, low-pressure space to grow your professional network and learn how to follow up the right way.
Come for the conversation; leave with contacts.
RSVP by April 10 at www.momentummeetup.dreyer.edu.

reading.title: The Benefits of Music Education
reading.prompt: Why does the author mention “neural pathways associated with attention and processing”?
reading.promptZh: 作者提及“与注意力和信息处理相关的神经通路”的原因是什么？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
In the United States, music education has been consistently linked to enhanced cognitive development. Studies such as those by the National Association for Music Education (NAfME) and research published in Frontiers in Psychology have shown that children who study music often demonstrate improvements in memory, language acquisition, and spatial-temporal reasoning. These cognitive gains are attributed to the discipline and structured practice inherent in learning music, which strengthens neural pathways associated with attention and processing.

Paragraph 2
Beyond cognition, music education contributes meaningfully to social development. Participation in an ensemble—a group of musicians performing together—requires active collaboration, listening, and nonverbal communication, fostering empathy and cooperative behavior. This group dynamic differs from traditional classroom settings and can support the development of interpersonal skills. Moreover, music provides a safe space for emotional exploration. Students engage with complex emotions, both their own and those conveyed by others, through the expressive nature of music itself. This experience can enhance emotional intelligence and serve as a constructive outlet for stress.

Paragraph 3
Despite these documented benefits, music programs in U.S. schools are often viewed as nonessential compared to core academic subjects and thus vulnerable to budget cuts. This reduction may disproportionately affect students who could benefit most from music’s holistic contributions, potentially limiting their cognitive, social, and emotional growth.

reading.translation:
作者提及“与注意力和信息处理相关的神经通路”的原因是什么？

在美国，音乐教育一直与增强的认知发展相联系。全国音乐教育协会（NAfME）的研究以及《Frontiers in Psychology》上发表的研究显示，学习音乐的儿童常在记忆、语言习得与时空推理上表现改善。这些认知收益被归因于学音乐所固有的纪律与结构化练习，它们强化与注意与加工相关的神经通路。
在认知之外，音乐教育对社会发展也有切实贡献。参与合奏——一群音乐家共同演奏——需要积极协作、倾听与非言语沟通，培养共情与合作行为。这种群体动态有别于传统课堂，可支持人际技能发展。此外，音乐为情绪探索提供安全空间：学生通过音乐本身的表达性，接触自己与他人所传达的复杂情绪。这种体验可增强情绪智力，并成为压力的建设性出口。
尽管这些益处有据可查，美国学校的音乐项目常被视为相对核心学科非必要，因而易受预算削减冲击。这种削减可能不成比例地影响最能从音乐整体贡献中受益的学生，潜在限制其认知、社会与情绪成长。

reading.title: The Benefits of Music Education
reading.prompt: Based on the discussion in the passage, what type of musical activity would be least likely to support social development?
reading.promptZh: 根据文章讨论，以下哪种音乐活动最不可能促进社会发展？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
In the United States, music education has been consistently linked to enhanced cognitive development. Studies such as those by the National Association for Music Education (NAfME) and research published in Frontiers in Psychology have shown that children who study music often demonstrate improvements in memory, language acquisition, and spatial-temporal reasoning. These cognitive gains are attributed to the discipline and structured practice inherent in learning music, which strengthens neural pathways associated with attention and processing.

Paragraph 2
Beyond cognition, music education contributes meaningfully to social development. Participation in an ensemble—a group of musicians performing together—requires active collaboration, listening, and nonverbal communication, fostering empathy and cooperative behavior. This group dynamic differs from traditional classroom settings and can support the development of interpersonal skills. Moreover, music provides a safe space for emotional exploration. Students engage with complex emotions, both their own and those conveyed by others, through the expressive nature of music itself. This experience can enhance emotional intelligence and serve as a constructive outlet for stress.

Paragraph 3
Despite these documented benefits, music programs in U.S. schools are often viewed as nonessential compared to core academic subjects and thus vulnerable to budget cuts. This reduction may disproportionately affect students who could benefit most from music’s holistic contributions, potentially limiting their cognitive, social, and emotional growth.

These [6] act_______ release [7] ga___ that [8] tr__ heat, [9] cau____ the [10] pla___ to warm up. This warming disrupts weather patterns and ecosystems. It results from changes in Earth's [1] atmos_____, oceans, [2] a__ human [3] activ_____, especially [4] bur____ fossil [5] fu___. These [6] act_______ release [7] ga___ that [8] tr__ heat, [9] cau____ the [10] pla___ to warm up. This warming disrupts weather patterns and ecosystems. reading.answer:
1. phere → atmosphere
2. nd → and
3. ities → activities
4. ning → burning
5. els → fuels
6. ivities → activities
7. ses → gases
8. ap → trap
9. sing → causing
10. net → planet
reading.explanation: 1. 在'Earth's'后，表示地球的大气层，是气候变化的三大要素之一，与后文' oceans'并列。 2. 用于连接'oceans'和'human activities'，表示并列关系，完整列出变化来源。 3. 指人类活动，尤其是后文提到的燃烧化石燃料，是气候变化的直接原因。 4. 指燃烧化石燃料这一具体活动，是人类活动中的关键行为。 5. 指化石燃料，是燃烧的对象，常见如煤炭、石油和天然气。 6. 指代前文的人类活动，这些活动释放气体，是导致变暖的环节。 7. 指释放的气体，这些气体能捕获热量，是温室效应的关键。 8. 指气体捕获热量的作用，这是温室气体导致地球变暖的机制。 9. 表示导致的结果，即前文活动引起地球变暖的直接影响。 10. 指地球，是变暖的主体，与前文'Earth's'呼应，强调全球性问题。
reading.translation: 气候变化是当今世界面临的最大问题之一。它源于地球大气、海洋与人类活动的变化，尤其是燃烧化石燃料。这些活动释放截留热量的气体，导致行星变暖。这种变暖扰乱天气模式与生态系统。为减轻这些变化，科学家主张减少碳排放并投资可再生能源等策略。气候模型帮助专家理解未来可能发生的情况。

reading.title: The New Dimensions of Choreography
reading.prompt: The word “profound” in the passage is closest in meaning to
reading.promptZh: 文中的“profound”一词最接近的含义是
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Choreography (the composition and arrangement of dance), once a ceremonial and courtly discipline rooted in ritualistic precision, has undergone a profound metamorphosis shaped by cultural shifts and artistic redefinition. Initially governed by strict formalism—particularly in classical ballet—it emphasized symmetry, control, and hierarchy. However, the 20th century witnessed a radical departure from these conventions. Visionaries like Martha Graham redefined dance as a medium for emotional expression and psychological depth, challenging ballet’s aesthetic rigidity and introducing vocabularies of movement that embraced tension, release, and groundedness, which emphasizes a strong connection to the earth or floor. This evolution marked a transition from spectacle to narrative, with choreography becoming a conduit for storytelling and social commentary.

Paragraph 2
Today, choreography increasingly reflects a decentralization of artistic authority. 【位置 1】 Rather than a single choreographer dictating movement, many contemporary works emerge from collaborative processes among dancers, composers, designers, and digital artists. 【位置 2】 This co-creative model not only democratizes authorship but also fosters performances that are adaptive and responsive—sometimes even improvised or altered in real time. The boundaries between creator and performer blur, yielding works that resist fixed interpretation. 【位置 3】 In this context, choreography becomes less a finished product and more a living dialogue among disciplines, identities, and ideas. 【位置 4】

reading.translation:
文中的“profound”一词最接近的含义是

编舞（舞蹈的构图与编排）曾是植根于仪式精确性的宫廷与礼仪学科，后在文化变迁与艺术重新定义下经历深刻蜕变。起初受严格形式主义支配——尤其在古典芭蕾中——强调对称、控制与等级。然而二十世纪见证了对这些惯例的激进背离。玛莎·格雷厄姆等先驱把舞蹈重塑为情绪表达与心理深度的媒介，挑战芭蕾的审美僵化，并引入拥抱张力、释放与「接地感」（强调与地面的牢固连接）的动作语汇。这一演进标志着从奇观向叙事的过渡，编舞成为讲故事与社会评论的通道。
今天，编舞日益体现艺术权威的去中心化。许多当代作品并非由单一编舞家规定动作，而由舞者、作曲家、设计师与数字艺术家协作产生。这种共创模式不仅使作者身份更民主，也催生可适应、可响应的表演——有时甚至即兴或实时改动。创作者与表演者的边界模糊，作品抗拒固定解读。在此语境下，编舞更少像成品，而更像学科、身份与观念之间活生生的对话。

reading.translation:
以下哪项最能描述编舞随时间的演变？

编舞（舞蹈的构图与编排）曾是植根于仪式精确性的宫廷与礼仪学科，后在文化变迁与艺术重新定义下经历深刻蜕变。起初受严格形式主义支配——尤其在古典芭蕾中——强调对称、控制与等级。然而二十世纪见证了对这些惯例的激进背离。玛莎·格雷厄姆等先驱把舞蹈重塑为情绪表达与心理深度的媒介，挑战芭蕾的审美僵化，并引入拥抱张力、释放与「接地感」（强调与地面的牢固连接）的动作语汇。这一演进标志着从奇观向叙事的过渡，编舞成为讲故事与社会评论的通道。
今天，编舞日益体现艺术权威的去中心化。许多当代作品并非由单一编舞家规定动作，而由舞者、作曲家、设计师与数字艺术家协作产生。这种共创模式不仅使作者身份更民主，也催生可适应、可响应的表演——有时甚至即兴或实时改动。创作者与表演者的边界模糊，作品抗拒固定解读。在此语境下，编舞更少像成品，而更像学科、身份与观念之间活生生的对话。

reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Choreography (the composition and arrangement of dance), once a ceremonial and courtly discipline rooted in ritualistic precision, has undergone a profound metamorphosis shaped by cultural shifts and artistic redefinition. Initially governed by strict formalism—particularly in classical ballet—it emphasized symmetry, control, and hierarchy. However, the 20th century witnessed a radical departure from these conventions. Visionaries like Martha Graham redefined dance as a medium for emotional expression and psychological depth, challenging ballet’s aesthetic rigidity and introducing vocabularies of movement that embraced tension, release, and groundedness, which emphasizes a strong connection to the earth or floor. This evolution marked a transition from spectacle to narrative, with choreography becoming a conduit for storytelling and social commentary.

Paragraph 2
Today, choreography increasingly reflects a decentralization of artistic authority. 【位置 1】 Rather than a single choreographer dictating movement, many contemporary works emerge from collaborative processes among dancers, composers, designers, and digital artists. 【位置 2】 This co-creative model not only democratizes authorship but also fosters performances that are adaptive and responsive—sometimes even improvised or altered in real time. The boundaries between creator and performer blur, yielding works that resist fixed interpretation. 【位置 3】 In this context, choreography becomes less a finished product and more a living dialogue among disciplines, identities, and ideas. 【位置 4】

listening.answer: C. To visualize how people relate and interact in a group

A. 社会图不测量个人智力。

B. 讲座开头强调 social networks 不只指数字平台，社会图也不限于线上交流。

listening.translation: 根据讲座内容，社会关系图的主要用途是什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a sociology podcast.
Social networks are not just digital online platforms. They're fundamental to understanding how people connect and interact. One powerful tool for analyzing these networks is the sociogram. A sociogram is a visual map that charts relationships within a group. It looks a little like a spider's web. Sociograms illustrate who interacts with whom, how frequently, and in what patterns. And by making invisible social structures visible, they reveal dynamics such as influence, isolation, and centrality. Rather than focusing on individual behavior as traditional studies would, sociograms emphasize the web of connections that shape group outcomes. In classrooms, they can identify students who are socially isolated or those who act as bridges between different social groups. In workplaces, sociograms help uncover informal hierarchies and where communication breaks down. In public health, they're used to trace contact patterns and predict how diseases might spread from person to person. Sociograms are valuable in marketing as well, where understanding who influences purchasing decisions can guide advertising strategy. However, sociograms do have limitations. By reducing relationships to lines in a web of interactions, they may overlook the subtleties of human interaction, such as trust, conflict, or emotional intensity that aren't easily captured in a diagram. Understanding these qualitative aspects often requires complementary methods like interviews or observation to fully appreciate. Still, when used thoughtfully and alongside other tools, sociograms remain a vital resource for visualizing and analyzing social networks. Their strength lies in turning abstract social dynamics into concrete, interpretable visuals, making them indispensable across disciplines.

Listen to part of a talk on a science podcast.
Have you ever experienced a sudden change in mood after you eat a meal? It's plausible that your gut microbiome played a role in that emotional shift. 

Okay, so the microbiome is an intricate network of bacteria, fungi, and various other microorganisms. Trillions of these tiny entities make up your microbiome. In recent years, our understanding of the microbiome has greatly expanded. We used to think of microbes primarily as pathogens, but we now recognize that microbes play an essential role in our health. 

Right. So these microbes are integral to your health, influencing your immune system. A diverse microbiome acts as an implicit defense mechanism, strengthening the immune system against potential pathogens that could be harmful. And recent studies underscore the significance of a gut microbiome in how our bodies respond to infections and even in shaping emotions. 

Microbes in the gut synthesize neurotransmitters, chemical messengers, such as serotonin. And you probably know serotonin, right? Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that influences our emotional state. This interaction between the gut and the central nervous system reveals a dynamic relationship. You could even think of it like a finely tuned orchestra. 

As research into the microbiome advances, the possibility of manipulating gut microbes as a medical treatment, from addressing autoimmune conditions to enhancing mental health, becomes increasingly likely. So you might even imagine a scenario where doctors prescribe personalized probiotic regimens tailored specifically to your unique microbiome. This would be a fundamental change that could redefine personalized medicine.

请听科学播客讲座的一部分。

好，微生物群是细菌、真菌与各种其他微生物的复杂网络。数万亿这些微小实体构成你的微生物群。近年来，我们对微生物群的理解大大扩展。我们过去主要把微生物看作病原体，但现在认识到微生物在健康中扮演关键角色。

对。这些微生物对你的健康不可或缺，影响免疫系统。多样的微生物群充当隐性防御机制，增强免疫系统对抗可能有害的潜在病原体。最近研究强调肠道微生物群在身体如何应对感染乃至塑造情绪方面的重要性。

肠道中的微生物合成神经递质——化学信使，如血清素。你大概知道血清素，对吧？血清素是影响情绪状态的神经递质。肠道与中枢神经系统之间的这种互动揭示一种动态关系。你甚至可以把它想成一支调校精良的管弦乐队。

随着对微生物群研究推进，操控肠道微生物作为医疗手段——从应对自身免疫状况到增强心理健康——的可能性越来越大。因此你甚至可以想象医生开出专门针对你独特微生物群的个性化益生菌方案。这将是可能重新定义个性化医疗的根本变化。

listening.translation: 演讲者为什么提到进食后出现的情绪波动？
listening.transcript:
Listen to part of a talk on a science podcast.
Have you ever experienced a sudden change in mood after you eat a meal? It's plausible that your gut microbiome played a role in that emotional shift. 

Okay, so the microbiome is an intricate network of bacteria, fungi, and various other microorganisms. Trillions of these tiny entities make up your microbiome. In recent years, our understanding of the microbiome has greatly expanded. We used to think of microbes primarily as pathogens, but we now recognize that microbes play an essential role in our health. 

Right. So these microbes are integral to your health, influencing your immune system. A diverse microbiome acts as an implicit defense mechanism, strengthening the immune system against potential pathogens that could be harmful. And recent studies underscore the significance of a gut microbiome in how our bodies respond to infections and even in shaping emotions. 

Microbes in the gut synthesize neurotransmitters, chemical messengers, such as serotonin. And you probably know serotonin, right? Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that influences our emotional state. This interaction between the gut and the central nervous system reveals a dynamic relationship. You could even think of it like a finely tuned orchestra. 

As research into the microbiome advances, the possibility of manipulating gut microbes as a medical treatment, from addressing autoimmune conditions to enhancing mental health, becomes increasingly likely. So you might even imagine a scenario where doctors prescribe personalized probiotic regimens tailored specifically to your unique microbiome. This would be a fundamental change that could redefine personalized medicine.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听科学播客讲座的一部分。
你是否曾在用餐后经历情绪突然变化？肠道微生物群在那次情绪转变中起作用是合理的。

好，微生物群是细菌、真菌与各种其他微生物的复杂网络。数万亿这些微小实体构成你的微生物群。近年来，我们对微生物群的理解大大扩展。我们过去主要把微生物看作病原体，但现在认识到微生物在健康中扮演关键角色。

对。这些微生物对你的健康不可或缺，影响免疫系统。多样的微生物群充当隐性防御机制，增强免疫系统对抗可能有害的潜在病原体。最近研究强调肠道微生物群在身体如何应对感染乃至塑造情绪方面的重要性。

肠道中的微生物合成神经递质——化学信使，如血清素。你大概知道血清素，对吧？血清素是影响情绪状态的神经递质。肠道与中枢神经系统之间的这种互动揭示一种动态关系。你甚至可以把它想成一支调校精良的管弦乐队。

随着对微生物群研究推进，操控肠道微生物作为医疗手段——从应对自身免疫状况到增强心理健康——的可能性越来越大。因此你甚至可以想象医生开出专门针对你独特微生物群的个性化益生菌方案。这将是可能重新定义个性化医疗的根本变化。

Woman: I will. I loved the book. I can't wait to discuss it. Nathan Cho is now officially one of my favorite authors.
Man: Wait a minute. Did you read Subtle Changes? That's on the schedule for next month.
Woman: Oh no! I must have read the wrong book.
Man: Well, on the bright side, Carver's Canyon is only 150 pages, and you've still got two days.
Woman: I know what I'll be doing tonight.

女：来。那本书我很喜欢。等不及讨论。Nathan Cho 现在正式是我最喜欢的作者之一。
男：等等。你读的是《Subtle Changes》？那是下个月的安排。
女：糟了！我肯定读错书了。
男：好在《Carver's Canyon》只有一百五十页，你还有两天。
女：我知道今晚要干什么了。

listening.translation: 讲座主要关于什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a geography class.

Woman: Urbanization is frequently associated with negative outcomes: pollution, overcrowding, and especially traffic congestion. In many cities, poor planning has led to increased noise and emissions as well as reduced quality of life. However, urbanization doesn't have to be this way. If approached thoughtfully, an alternative to traffic jams and congested city streets is to foster sustainable transportation. Copenhagen in Denmark, for instance, has made bicycles a central part of its urban design. The city's extensive network of protected bike lanes and pro cycling policies have encouraged residents to choose bicycles over cars. In addition to lowering automobile emissions, this shift has also improved public health and reduced traffic related stress. Also, when kept in control and planned properly, urbanization, in this case compact urban living, minimizes land use and energy consumption. Compared to sprawling suburban development, suburban neighborhoods require large plots of land for individual homes, roads and parking. When housing, services and infrastructure are concentrated, this can actually preserve surrounding natural areas and agricultural lands. So, even though this may seem strange, urban growth is actually more compatible with environmental conservation. Urbanization also, by necessity, has led to some innovative thinking, especially concerning the efficient use of land and space. Many cities are incorporating such innovation in food production by creating rooftop farms and using vertical agriculture, which grows crops in stacked vertical layers. In particular, Singapore has invested in high tech urban farming systems that grow vegetables in controlled environments, helping increase local food supply and reduce dependence on imports.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段地理课的讲座。

女：城市化常与负面结果联系在一起：污染、过度拥挤，尤其是交通拥堵。在许多城市，糟糕的规划导致噪音与排放增加、生活质量下降。但城市化不必如此。若用心处理，替代堵车与拥挤街道的办法是培育可持续交通。例如丹麦哥本哈根把自行车作为城市设计的核心。该市广泛的受保护自行车道网络与支持骑行的政策鼓励居民选自行车而非汽车。除降低汽车排放外，这一转变也改善了公共健康、减少了与交通相关的压力。此外，在受控并妥善规划时，城市化——此处指紧凑城市生活——可最小化土地使用与能源消耗。与蔓延的郊区开发相比，郊区社区需要大块土地用于独栋住宅、道路与停车。当住房、服务与基础设施集中时，实际上可保护周边自然区与农地。因此，尽管可能显得奇怪，城市增长其实更与环境保护相容。城市化也因必要而催生一些创新思维，尤其关于土地与空间的高效利用。许多城市把这种创新纳入粮食生产，创建屋顶农场并使用垂直农业——在叠放的垂直层中种植作物。特别是新加坡投资高科技城市农业系统，在受控环境中种植蔬菜，有助增加本地粮食供应、减少对进口的依赖。

女：城市化常与负面结果联系在一起：污染、过度拥挤，尤其是交通拥堵。在许多城市，糟糕的规划导致噪音与排放增加、生活质量下降。但城市化不必如此。若用心处理，替代堵车与拥挤街道的办法是培育可持续交通。例如丹麦哥本哈根把自行车作为城市设计的核心。该市广泛的受保护自行车道网络与支持骑行的政策鼓励居民选自行车而非汽车。除降低汽车排放外，这一转变也改善了公共健康、减少了与交通相关的压力。此外，在受控并妥善规划时，城市化——此处指紧凑城市生活——可最小化土地使用与能源消耗。与蔓延的郊区开发相比，郊区社区需要大块土地用于独栋住宅、道路与停车。当住房、服务与基础设施集中时，实际上可保护周边自然区与农地。因此，尽管可能显得奇怪，城市增长其实更与环境保护相容。城市化也因必要而催生一些创新思维，尤其关于土地与空间的高效利用。许多城市把这种创新纳入粮食生产，创建屋顶农场并使用垂直农业——在叠放的垂直层中种植作物。特别是新加坡投资高科技城市农业系统，在受控环境中种植蔬菜，有助增加本地粮食供应、减少对进口的依赖。

listening.transcript: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Expressionism is an influential modernist art movement that emerged in the early 20th century. This movement is characterized by its focus on representing emotional experience rather than physical reality. Expressionist artists aim to convey their inner feelings and perceptions through distorted and exaggerated forms, vivid colors, and bold brushstrokes. One of the most famous Expressionist artists is Edvard Munch. His painting The Scream shows an agonized person crying out. It eventually became an icon of the movement's focus on intense personal experience. Expressionism was not limited to visual arts, however. It also influenced literature, theater and cinematic arts. In literature, authors like Franz Kafka explored themes of alienation and existential angst. Expressionist theater often used dramatic lighting and intense performances to evoke emotional responses. Sets sometimes featured oversized symbolic objects. In Elmer Rice's 1923 play The Adding Machine, a giant adding machine represents the dehumanizing forces of technology. Similarly, German Expressionist film used innovative techniques. Despite its impact, Expressionism faced criticism for departure from traditional aesthetics and emphasis on the personal. Critics argued that its focus on subjective emotion robbed works of broader content or meaning. Nonetheless, Expressionism paved the way for later movements such as Surrealism.
listening.transcriptZh: 请听一段艺术史课的讲座。表现主义是二十世纪初兴起的有影响力的现代主义艺术运动。其特点是侧重表现情感体验而非物理现实。表现主义艺术家通过变形夸张的形态、鲜明色彩与大胆笔触，传达内心感受与知觉。最著名的表现主义艺术家之一是爱德华·蒙克。他的画作《呐喊》呈现一个痛苦呼号的人。它最终成为该运动强调强烈个人体验的标志。但表现主义不限于视觉艺术。它也影响文学、戏剧与电影。文学上，弗兰茨·卡夫卡等作家探索异化与存在焦虑主题。表现主义戏剧常用戏剧性灯光与强烈表演唤起情感反应。布景有时出现超大号象征物件。在埃尔默·赖斯一九二三年的剧作《加法机》中，一台巨大的加法机代表技术的非人化力量。同样，德国表现主义电影使用创新手法。尽管影响巨大，表现主义因偏离传统美学、强调个人而受批评。批评者认为它对主观情感的聚焦剥夺了作品更广的内容或意义。尽管如此，表现主义为超现实主义等后来运动铺了路。

content.promptText: Thank you for agreeing to participate. I'd like to ask you some questions about remote work. First, do you prefer to work remotely? How often would you prefer to work remotely?

speaking.answer: I would prefer to work remotely two or three days a week, not every single day. Uh, I like the quiet environment at home because I can focus better on tasks like writing reports or answering emails. Also, I save a lot of time when I don't have to commute, and that extra time can be used for exercise or sleep. However, I still think going to the office sometimes is useful. You know, face-to-face conversations make it easier to build trust with coworkers and solve problems quickly. So for me, a mixed schedule would be the most comfortable and productive arrangement, especially during a busy school or work week.

content.promptText: Thank you. What challenges or difficulties do you think remote work may involve?

speaking.answer: One challenge of remote work is communication. When people are not in the same place, a small misunderstanding can last longer because nobody can just walk over and ask a quick question. Um, another difficulty is staying motivated. At home, there are many distractions, like family members, chores, or even the temptation to take a longer break than planned. I also think some workers may feel lonely if they rarely meet their teammates in person. Honestly, remote work sounds convenient, but it requires strong self-discipline and clear communication rules. Without those, it can become confusing and inefficient pretty quickly, even for responsible employees, in my opinion.
speaking.translation: 谢谢。你认为远程工作可能涉及哪些挑战或困难？

speaking.prompt: I see. Do you think companies should ensure fairness when giving employees remote-work opportunities? Why or why not?

content.promptText: I see. Do you think companies should ensure fairness when giving employees remote-work opportunities? Why or why not?

speaking.answer: Yes, I think companies should, because unfair rules can really hurt team spirit. Um, imagine two employees doing similar jobs, but only one is allowed to work from home. The other person would probably feel upset and less motivated to do their best. Fairness doesn't have to mean everyone gets exactly the same, though. Some jobs, like those in a factory or a store, simply can't be done remotely. But when the work is possible online, the company should set clear rules, like performance or role, and apply them to everyone. I mean, people trust a workplace more when decisions are open and consistent. Honestly, that trust makes employees work harder, so fairness benefits the company as well, not just the workers.
speaking.translation: 明白了。你认为公司在给予员工远程工作机会时应该确保公平性吗？为什么？

content.promptText: Great. Do you think remote work will become a mainstream trend in the future? Why or why not?

speaking.answer: I think it'll become more common, but I'm not sure it'll fully become mainstream. Uh, since the pandemic, many companies have discovered that people can do a lot of work from home, and it saves money on office space. Workers like it too, because they skip long commutes and gain flexibility. Technology will keep getting better, so meetings online will feel more natural over the next few years. But some jobs need face-to-face teamwork, and a lot of people miss social contact at the office. So I expect a mix, with a few days at home and a few days at the office. That hybrid style seems like the most realistic future to me, rather than everyone working from their living room all the time.

content.promptText: Your professor is teaching a class on communications. Write a post responding to the professor's question.
content.stimulusText: Your professor is teaching a class on communications. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion. Make a contribution to the discussion in your own words. An effective response will contain at least 100 words. We've been discussing the role of storytelling in effective communication. Storytelling can be a powerful tool to convey messages and connect with audiences emotionally. Some experts argue that storytelling is essential for engaging presentations, while others believe that factual, straightforward communication is more effective. What is your opinion on the use of storytelling in communication?
content.post: Paul: Factual, straightforward communication is more effective. Clear and concise information ensures that the audience understands the message without any ambiguity. While stories can be engaging, they may sometimes distract from the main points. Successful communication is determined more by its ability to convey a message than it is to entertain an audience.

writing.answer:
I believe storytelling is essential for effective communication, especially when a speaker wants people to remember and care about an idea. Facts are important, but facts alone can feel distant. A well-chosen story gives information a human context, which helps the audience understand why the message matters. For example, a presentation about public health becomes more memorable if it includes a patient’s experience rather than only statistics.

Paul makes a fair point that communication should be clear and not distracted by unnecessary details. However, good storytelling does not replace facts; it organizes them in a way that feels meaningful. The key is to use stories that directly support the main point. When speakers combine accurate information with relevant stories, they can be both clear and emotionally engaging. For this reason, I think storytelling is a powerful part of successful communication.

Dr. Gupta：我们一直在讨论讲故事在有效沟通中的作用。讲故事可以成为传达信息和在情感上连接观众的有力工具。一些专家认为讲故事对于吸引人的演讲至关重要，而另一些专家则认为事实性的、直截了当的沟通更有效。你对在沟通中使用讲故事有何看法？

Kelly：讲故事对于成功沟通至关重要，例如在演讲中。它有助于在情感层面与观众建立联系，使信息更令人难忘和具有影响力。故事可以比单纯的事实更生动地说明观点，并从头到尾保持观众的参与度。

Paul：事实性的、直截了当的沟通更有效。清晰简洁的信息确保观众理解信息而没有任何歧义。虽然故事可能引人入胜，但有时可能会分散对主要观点的注意力。成功沟通的决定性因素在于传达信息的能力，而非娱乐观众的能力。

reading.title: Baroque to Classical Music
reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
reading.passage: The transition from Baroque to Classical music reflected broader cultural shifts in eighteenth-century Europe. Baroque music, with its elaborate textures and emotional intensity, mirrored the grandeur of monarchies and the Church. As Enlightenment [1] ide__ gained [2] infl_____, Classical music [3] eme____ with [4] sim____, less [5] orn___ structures, [6] bala____ phrasing, and a [7] fo___ on [8] rea___ and [9] or___. Composers [10] li__ Haydn and Mozart embraced simplicity and symmetry, aligning with the era's intellectual and political movements that favored rational thought over divine authority. This stylistic shift marked a move toward accessibility and elegance in musical expression.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: The transition from Baroque to Classical music reflected broader cultural shifts in eighteenth-century Europe. Baroque music, with its elaborate textures and emotional intensity, mirrored the grandeur of monarchies and the Church. As Enlightenment [1] ide__ gained [2] infl_____, Classical music [3] eme____ with [4] sim____, less [5] orn___ structures, [6] bala____ phrasing, and a [7] fo___ on [8] rea___ and [9] or___. Composers [10] li__ Haydn and Mozart embraced simplicity and symmetry, aligning with the era's intellectual and political movements that favored rational thought over divine authority. This stylistic shift marked a move toward accessibility and elegance in musical expression.

reading.answer:
1. as → ideas
2. uence → influence
3. rged → emerged
4. pler → simpler
5. ate → ornate
6. nced → balanced
7. cus → focus
8. son → reason
9. der → order
10. ke → like
reading.explanation: 1. Enlightenment 后需要名词，ideas 表示启蒙思想，与下文 gained influence 搭配。 2. gained 后接名词 influence，gained influence 是固定搭配，表示获得影响力。 3. Classical music 后需要动词，emerged 表示出现，与 transition from Baroque 呼应。 4. 与 ornate 对比，simpler 表示更简单的结构，是古典音乐的特征。 5. ornate 表示华丽的，与巴洛克音乐的 elaborate textures 对应。 6. balanced 修饰 phrasing，表示平衡的乐句，体现古典音乐的秩序。 7. a focus on 是固定短语，表示关注，这里指音乐的重点。 8. 与 order 并列，reason 表示理性，启蒙运动的核心思想。 9. 与 reason 并列，order 表示秩序，强调理性思维。 10. like 用于举例，引出具体作曲家 Haydn 和 Mozart。
reading.translation: 从巴洛克到古典音乐的过渡反映了十八世纪欧洲更广泛的文化变迁。巴洛克音乐以其精致织体与情感强度，映照君主制与教会的宏伟。随着启蒙思想获得影响，古典音乐以更简单、不那么华丽的结构、平衡乐句以及对理性与秩序的聚焦而出现。海顿与莫扎特等作曲家拥抱简洁与对称，与那个时代偏爱理性思想而非神权的智识与政治运动对齐。这一风格转变标志着音乐表达向可及与优雅的迈进。

Pigments, the materials that give color to paint, are [1] der____ from [2] var____ sources, [3] incl_____ minerals, [4] pla___, and [5] synt_____ compounds. [6] Art____ selected [7] mate_____ based [8] o_ their [9] abi____ to [10] con____ underlying layers (opacity) and resist fading over time. The transformation of pigments into vibrant colors involves the complex interaction of light with the pigment's molecular structure. This interaction determines the color's intensity and luminosity.

reading.answer:
1. ived → derived
2. ious → various
3. uding → including
4. nts → plants
5. hetic → synthetic
6. ists → Artists
7. rials → materials
8. n → on
9. lity → ability
10. ceal → conceal
reading.explanation: 1. are derived from 是固定短语，表示“源自”，这里指颜料源自矿物、植物等各种来源。 2. various 修饰 sources，表示“各种各样的”，强调颜料来源的多样性。 3. including 用于引出具体例子，这里列出矿物、植物等来具体说明颜料的来源。 4. plants 与 minerals 和 synthetic compounds 并列，指植物作为颜料来源之一。 5. synthetic 表示“合成的”，指人工合成的化合物，与其他自然来源形成对比。 6. Artists 是句子主语，指艺术家，他们根据颜料特性选择材料。 7. materials 是 selected 的宾语，表示“材料”，指艺术家选择的颜料材料。 8. on 与 based 构成固定搭配 based on，表示“基于”，这里指基于能力来选择。 9. ability 是名词，their 后接名词，ability to do sth. 表示“做某事的能力”，这里指遮盖底层的能力。 10. conceal 表示“遮盖”，与 underlying layers 搭配，指颜料能遮盖底层以形成不透明效果。
reading.translation: 在视觉艺术中，色彩与颜料的互动对塑造艺术表达至关重要。颜料是为油漆赋予颜色的材料，来自矿物、植物与合成化合物等多种来源。艺术家根据掩盖底层（不透明度）与抗褪色能力选择材料。颜料转化为鲜艳色彩涉及光与颜料分子结构的复杂互动。这一互动决定颜色的强度与光泽。

reading.title: Surprise Arts Week Dance Performance
reading.prompt: What is the main topic of the article?
reading.promptZh: 这篇文章的主旨是什么？
reading.passage: At noon yesterday, Summit View University's quad suddenly erupted into music as fifty dance majors performed a surprise choreographed routine to celebrate Arts Week. “We wanted to bring joy and energy,” said organizer Leah Ogorzelec, who spent two weeks planning the event in secret. “By all accounts, we succeeded!” Students gathered in droves, cheering and filming the spectacle. “It made my day,” said freshman Ryan Patel, who shared the video on social media. Within hours, clips of the flash mob were trending, earning thousands of likes and comments. The performance ended with a dramatic group pose and applause echoing across campus. “It's all about making art accessible to everyone,” Ms. Ogorzelec explained. Faculty praised the creativity of the event, calling it a perfect kickoff to Arts Week. The event has sparked conversations about adding more spontaneous art experiences to campus life, proving that a little rhythm can unite an entire community.

这篇文章的主旨是什么？

昨天中午，顶峰景观大学四方院突然响起音乐，五十名舞蹈专业学生表演惊喜编舞，庆祝艺术周。「我们想带来欢乐与活力，」秘密筹划两周的组织者莉娅·奥戈泽莱茨说。「各方面看，我们成功了！」学生蜂拥聚集，欢呼并拍摄这一场面。「这让我一天都开心，」大一新生瑞安·帕特尔说，他把视频发到社交媒体。几小时内，快闪片段热传，获得数千点赞与评论。表演以戏剧性的集体造型与响彻校园的掌声结束。「关键是让艺术人人可及，」奥戈泽莱茨女士解释。教师称赞活动创意，称其为艺术周的完美开场。该活动引发关于在校园生活中增加更多即兴艺术体验的讨论，证明一点节奏就能团结整个社区。

reading.title: Cooperative Education
reading.prompt: The passage mentions all of the following about cooperative education programs EXCEPT:
reading.promptZh: 文章提到了关于合作教育项目的所有以下方面，除了：
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Cooperative education ("co-ops") emerged in the United States in the early twentieth century, when engineering programs seeking stronger industry alignment began alternating academic terms with structured, paid work experience. Although the model was first formalized at the University of Cincinnati, its rapid adoption across institutions specializing in scientific and technical fields reflected broader recognition that technical fields required applied practice alongside theoretical coursework. Today, co-ops are most prevalent at universities with deep employer partnerships. At Northeastern University and Drexel University, most students complete co-ops (multi-month paid placements) in fields ranging from engineering to computing to design. These programs often involve multiple sequenced work terms with increasing responsibility and are integrated into degree requirements rather than treated as optional internships.

Paragraph 2
Proponents argue that co-ops cultivate professional maturity by requiring students to navigate real organizational structures, contribute to long-term projects, and build evidence-based portfolios before graduation. They also note that co-op graduates often report higher initial earnings and stronger job placement. Critics, however, contend that alternating semesters can disrupt academic continuity, extend time-to-degree, and disadvantage students who cannot relocate or afford breaks in campus employment. Despite these concerns, co-op education remains a defining form of work-integrated learning, especially in fields where applied expertise is essential.

reading.translation:
文章提到了关于合作教育项目的所有以下方面，除了：

合作教育（co-ops）于二十世纪初在美国兴起：寻求与产业更紧密对齐的工程项目开始在学期与结构化、带薪工作经历之间交替。该模式虽首先在辛辛那提大学正式化，却迅速被专长于科学与技术领域的院校采纳，反映出更广泛的认识——技术领域需要理论课程之外的应用实践。今天，合作教育在与雇主深度合作的大学最为普遍。在东北大学与德雷塞尔大学，多数学生完成工程、计算到设计等领域的合作教育（为期数月的带薪实习）。这些项目往往包含责任递增的多段工作学期，并纳入学位要求，而非被视为可选实习。
支持者认为，合作教育通过要求学生在真实组织中导航、贡献长期项目并在毕业前建立有证据的作品集，培养职业成熟度。他们还指出，合作教育毕业生常报告更高的起薪与更强的就业安置。批评者则认为学期交替会打断学术连续性、延长修业时间，并不利于无法搬迁或负担不起校园就业中断的学生。尽管有这些关切，合作教育仍是工作整合学习的标志形式，尤其在应用专长至关重要的领域。

合作教育（co-ops）于二十世纪初在美国兴起：寻求与产业更紧密对齐的工程项目开始在学期与结构化、带薪工作经历之间交替。该模式虽首先在辛辛那提大学正式化，却迅速被专长于科学与技术领域的院校采纳，反映出更广泛的认识——技术领域需要理论课程之外的应用实践。今天，合作教育在与雇主深度合作的大学最为普遍。在东北大学与德雷塞尔大学，多数学生完成工程、计算到设计等领域的合作教育（为期数月的带薪实习）。这些项目往往包含责任递增的多段工作学期，并纳入学位要求，而非被视为可选实习。
支持者认为，合作教育通过要求学生在真实组织中导航、贡献长期项目并在毕业前建立有证据的作品集，培养职业成熟度。他们还指出，合作教育毕业生常报告更高的起薪与更强的就业安置。批评者则认为学期交替会打断学术连续性、延长修业时间，并不利于无法搬迁或负担不起校园就业中断的学生。尽管有这些关切，合作教育仍是工作整合学习的标志形式，尤其在应用专长至关重要的领域。

reading.title: Cooperative Education
reading.prompt: The word “cultivate” in the passage is closest in meaning to
reading.promptZh: 文章中“cultivate”一词最接近的意思是
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Cooperative education ("co-ops") emerged in the United States in the early twentieth century, when engineering programs seeking stronger industry alignment began alternating academic terms with structured, paid work experience. Although the model was first formalized at the University of Cincinnati, its rapid adoption across institutions specializing in scientific and technical fields reflected broader recognition that technical fields required applied practice alongside theoretical coursework. Today, co-ops are most prevalent at universities with deep employer partnerships. At Northeastern University and Drexel University, most students complete co-ops (multi-month paid placements) in fields ranging from engineering to computing to design. These programs often involve multiple sequenced work terms with increasing responsibility and are integrated into degree requirements rather than treated as optional internships.

Paragraph 2
Proponents argue that co-ops cultivate professional maturity by requiring students to navigate real organizational structures, contribute to long-term projects, and build evidence-based portfolios before graduation. They also note that co-op graduates often report higher initial earnings and stronger job placement. Critics, however, contend that alternating semesters can disrupt academic continuity, extend time-to-degree, and disadvantage students who cannot relocate or afford breaks in campus employment. Despite these concerns, co-op education remains a defining form of work-integrated learning, especially in fields where applied expertise is essential.

reading.title: Comparative Advantage and Trade
reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
reading.passage: In analyzing global trade dynamics, the principle of comparative advantage plays a foundational role. It suggests that nations should specialize in producing goods they can create most efficiently, thereby enhancing [1] ove____ economic [2] produc______ and [3] fost_____ international [4] interde________. However, [5] exce_____ reliance [6] o_ this [7] mo___ can [8] exp___ economies [9] t_ significant [10] ri___. Countries that concentrate on a limited range of exports may become vulnerable to market volatility, such as shifts in global demand or price fluctuations. While comparative advantage can stimulate growth, it must be strategically managed to ensure long-term economic sustainability.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: In analyzing global trade dynamics, the principle of comparative advantage plays a foundational role. It suggests that nations should specialize in producing goods they can create most efficiently, thereby enhancing [1] ove____ economic [2] produc______ and [3] fost_____ international [4] interde________. However, [5] exce_____ reliance [6] o_ this [7] mo___ can [8] exp___ economies [9] t_ significant [10] ri___. Countries that concentrate on a limited range of exports may become vulnerable to market volatility, such as shifts in global demand or price fluctuations. While comparative advantage can stimulate growth, it must be strategically managed to ensure long-term economic sustainability.

reading.answer:
1. rall → overall
2. tivity → productivity
3. ering → fostering
4. pendence → interdependence
5. ssive → excessive
6. n → on
7. del → model
8. ose → expose
9. o → to
10. sks → risks
reading.explanation: 1. overall：修饰 economic productivity，表示整体的经济生产力，强调全面效率提升，使句子表达全局性增强。 2. productivity：名词指生产能力，与 economic 搭配构成经济生产力，作为 enhancing 的宾语，完成短语含义。 3. fostering：动词-ing 形式，与 enhancing 并列，表示促进国际相互依赖，使句子结构平行且语义连贯。 4. interdependence：名词指相互依赖，这里描述国际间的经济互赖关系，作为 fostering 的宾语，呼应比较优势主题。 5. excessive：形容词修饰 reliance，表示过度依赖，对应后文风险，使逻辑转折更清晰。 6. on：介词与 reliance 固定搭配，表示对模型的依赖，完成短语 reliance on。 7. model：名词指模型，这里指前文的比较优势原则，作为代词 this 的指代对象。 8. expose：动词与 can 搭配，表示使暴露，指经济体可能面临风险，引出后果。 9. to：介词与 expose 固定搭配，表示暴露于，连接 exposure 和 risks。 10. risks：名词复数指风险，与 significant 搭配强调风险的显著性，作为 to 的宾语完成句子。
reading.translation: 在分析全球贸易动态时，比较优势原则起基础作用。它表明国家应专门生产它们能最有效创造的商品，从而提升整体经济生产率并促进国际相互依存。然而过度依赖这一模型可使经济暴露于重大风险。集中于有限出口范围的国家可能易受市场波动影响，例如全球需求转变或价格波动。虽然比较优势可刺激增长，必须战略管理以确保长期经济可持续。

reading.title: Universal Basic Income Debate
reading.prompt: What best characterizes UBI as described in the passage?
reading.promptZh: 根据文章内容，以下哪项最能概括全民基本收入（UBI）？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
The concept of universal basic income (UBI) is gaining attention worldwide. UBI provides all citizens with a regular, unconditional sum of money. Proponents argue that UBI can reduce poverty, streamline welfare, and offer a safety net in an era of automation and job loss. In Finland, a two-year pilot program gave 2,000 unemployed citizens a monthly payment. The results showed improved mental well-being and a modest increase in employment, but the findings were not definitive. Similarly, an experiment in Ontario, Canada, showed promising social benefits but was cut short due to cost concerns.

Paragraph 2
Critics raise several concerns. One major argument against UBI is its cost. Implementing it could require significant tax increases or reallocating government resources, straining public finances. There are also concerns about the impact on labor markets. Opponents suggest that a guaranteed income might disincentivize work, leading to reduced productivity and economic stagnation. The relationship between UBI and inflation is another common concern. While most pilot programs have not reported noticeable inflation in local prices, the programs are limited in scale and have not injected enough money into economies to significantly affect prices. Some economists note that certain sectors, like housing or groceries, could see localized price increases due to increased demand.

C. 错。文中恰好说多数试验没有报告明显的本地价格通胀，更没有 dramatic increase。

reading.translation:
关于全民基本收入（UBI）与通货膨胀，文章暗示了什么？

全民基本收入（UBI）这一概念正日益受到全球关注。UBI 向所有公民定期、无条件地发放一笔资金。支持者认为，UBI 可以减轻贫困、简化福利体系，并在自动化与失业加剧的时代提供安全网。在芬兰，一项为期两年的试点计划向 2000 名失业公民每月发放补助。结果显示心理健康有所改善，就业略有增加，但结论尚不具决定性。同样，加拿大安大略省的一项实验也显示出积极的社会效益，却因成本顾虑而提前终止。
批评者提出若干担忧。反对 UBI 的主要论点之一是成本：实施可能需要大幅增税或重新分配政府资源，从而给公共财政带来压力。对劳动力市场的影响也令人关切。反对者认为，有保障的收入可能削弱工作意愿，导致生产率下降与经济停滞。UBI 与通胀的关系是另一个常见顾虑。尽管多数试点并未报告当地物价出现明显上涨，但这些项目规模有限，注入经济的资金不足以显著影响价格。一些经济学家指出，住房或食品等某些行业可能因需求上升而出现局部涨价。

listening.translation: 演讲者主要讨论什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
Researchers are studying how sensory experiences can affect human behavior, like the use of ambient scent. Ambient scent is the strategic use of a certain fragrance, smell, in a space to set a specific mood, for example, or to cause people to associate a scent with a particular brand. Like a hotel chain, and each hotel's lobby smells like, say, pine trees. Customers experience that ambient scent every time they enter one of these hotels, and it can increase their loyalty to that hotel chain. One experiment involved participants in a room that smelled like freshly baked cookies, while others were in a scentless environment. Those who had the pleasant aroma around them were significantly more likely to volunteer for a charitable cause later. It's as if the warm and inviting scent triggered a sense of goodwill and community feeling in these participants. Why does this happen? Well, scents stimulate our limbic system. The limbic system is the part of the brain that's responsible for emotions and memory. So, fragrances can really make our brains connect with our emotional state and access our memories. When we encounter a comforting smell, like fresh bread, it might remind us of home or childhood, nudging us toward kindness and cooperation. The implications of this are intriguing, especially in marketing or organizational behavior. Imagine using lavender, which has a calming effect, in a high-pressure work environment. Something as simple as smell can have a profound effect on actions and decisions.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段心理学课的讲座。
研究者在研究感官体验如何影响人类行为，例如环境气味的使用。环境气味是在空间中策略性使用某种香气、气味，例如以营造特定心情，或让人把一种气味与特定品牌联系起来。像连锁酒店，每家酒店大堂都闻起来像，比方说，松树。顾客每次进入这些酒店都会体验到那种环境气味，这可增强他们对那家连锁的忠诚。一项实验中，参与者在闻起来像刚烤好曲奇的房间，另一些则在无味环境。周围有宜人香气的人后来显著更可能为慈善事业做志愿者。仿佛温暖诱人的气味触发了这些参与者的善意与社群感。为何如此？气味刺激我们的边缘系统。边缘系统是负责情绪与记忆的大脑部分。因此香气真能使大脑连接情绪状态并调动记忆。当我们遇到安慰性气味，如新鲜面包，它可能让我们想起家或童年，把我们推向善意与合作。其含义令人感兴趣，尤其在营销或组织行为中。想象在高压工作环境中使用有镇静效果的薰衣草。像气味这样简单的东西可对行动与决定产生深刻影响。

listening.transcript:

Researchers are studying how sensory experiences can affect human behavior, like the use of ambient scent. Ambient scent is the strategic use of a certain fragrance, smell, in a space to set a specific mood, for example, or to cause people to associate a scent with a particular brand. Like a hotel chain, and each hotel's lobby smells like, say, pine trees. Customers experience that ambient scent every time they enter one of these hotels, and it can increase their loyalty to that hotel chain. When we encounter a comforting smell, like fresh bread, it might remind us of home or childhood, nudging us toward kindness and cooperation.
