At that time, his major focus wasn't abstract expressionism, but social realism. Social realism refers to works that draw attention to socio-political issues. Maybe you've seen the painting American Gothic by Grant Wood, the one showing an older man and woman, farmers, standing in front of their home, looking very serious, and the man is holding a pitchfork? Anyway, Norman Lewis' social realist works focused on life in Harlem, New York City, where he lived. It also led him to be a member of a group of fellow black artists called the 306 Group. This is where we get into abstract expressionism. He focused on beauty and harmony in his art, and less on the political side of things as he had earlier. His painting, Migratory Birds, shows that. 说到抽象表现主义，你脑海里大概会浮现色彩斑斓、看起来很混乱的画布。你也许熟悉这个运动的领军人物杰克逊·波洛克。但诺曼·刘易斯呢？大概不熟。诺曼·刘易斯与抽象表现主义有关，不过当时关于这一运动的重要出版物并没有收录他。他的作品也卖得不好。要我说，这不公平。刘易斯得过奖，也受到评论家的认可。因此，直到他 1979 年去世之后，他的作品才真正被承认。刘易斯的职业生涯始于 1930 年。那时，他的主要关注点并不是抽象表现主义，而是社会现实主义。社会现实主义指的是那些把注意力引向社会政治问题的作品。你也许见过格兰特·伍德的画作《美国哥特式》，画面上是一对年长的男女农民，站在自家屋前，神情非常严肃，男人手里还拿着一把干草叉？总之，诺曼·刘易斯的社会现实主义作品聚焦于他生活的纽约哈莱姆区的生活。这也让他加入了一个由黑人艺术家组成的团体，叫做 306 团体。306 团体在哈莱姆一起工作。随着刘易斯事业的推进，大约在 1950 年，他的作品变得更加抽象。所以，大约从 1950 年起，刘易斯开始更关注艺术中的美与和谐。我们由此进入抽象表现主义。他在艺术中更强调美与和谐，而不再像早年那样侧重政治。他的画作《候鸟》就说明了这一点。画面是对鸟的抽象描绘，有纤细的白色笔触，背景则是橙棕色。

listening.translation: 说话人为什么提到一幅名叫《美国哥特式》、画着一对年长男女的作品？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an art history class.
When you think of abstract expressionism, you probably imagine colorful, chaotic canvases. Maybe you're familiar with Jackson Pollock, a leader of the movement. But how about Norman Lewis? Probably not. Norman Lewis is associated with abstract expressionism, although he wasn't included in major publications about the movement. Nor did his work sell very well. If you ask me, that's an injustice. Lewis won awards and was well regarded by critics. And so, he wasn't really recognized for his work until after his death in 1979. Lewis' career began in 1930. At that time, his major focus wasn't abstract expressionism, but social realism. Social realism refers to works that draw attention to socio-political issues. Maybe you've seen the painting American Gothic by Grant Wood, the one showing an older man and woman, farmers, standing in front of their home, looking very serious, and the man is holding a pitchfork? Anyway, Norman Lewis' social realist works focused on life in Harlem, New York City, where he lived. It also led him to be a member of a group of fellow black artists called the 306 Group. The 306 Group worked together in Harlem. As Lewis' career went on, around 1950, his work became more abstract. So, it's around 1950 that Lewis began focusing more on beauty and harmony in his art. This is where we get into abstract expressionism. He focused on beauty and harmony in his art, and less on the political side of things as he had earlier. His painting, Migratory Birds, shows that. There's an abstract depiction of birds with delicate white marks and an orange brown background.

listening.translation: 女生想做什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Woman: Sam, have you booked your flights for next month's conference yet?
Man: I just did. I found a good price actually.
Woman: Oh really? I haven't booked yet.
Man: I found mine using flight comparison websites. They show you the best price across different airlines.
Woman: That's a good idea. Yeah, I'll check a few of those.
Man: I also booked an early morning flight, which was cheaper, and if you have flexibility in your travel plans, I found it was cheaper to fly on Monday than on Tuesday, so I'm going to get there early and do some sightseeing before the conference starts.

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.
So there's an ancient invention, the Archimedes screw. The Archimedes screw is credited to the Greek mathematician Archimedes in about 250 BCE, although it's possible that, uh, ancient Egyptians were actually using it first. Archimedes might have learned about it from the Egyptians, but we don't really know.

Now, the Archimedes screw isn't something used to, like, assemble a piece of furniture. Picture a much larger screw than one for furniture. Like any screw, it has threads, the continuous ridge that spirals around it. The threads are one long spiral from one end of the screw to the other, okay? And that long screw fits inside the length of a long tube. That's the Archimedes screw. It's used to lift water from a low area up to higher ground. You'd put one end of it down into the low water and the other end up higher at an angle, not straight up and down, but at a more horizontal angle. Then turn it. Water gets into the tube and onto the threads. When you turn the screw, the water is transported upward.

This was an effective way, for example, to get water from rivers or lakes to irrigate fields for crops, an impactful technology in agriculture. Also, there's evidence that in ancient Spain, they used the Archimedes screw to pump water out of mines. Besides Spanish mines, it was used elsewhere to pump water out of ships in antiquity as well, and in wastewater treatment plants even today.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听历史课上的一段讲解。
有一种古代发明，叫阿基米德螺旋泵。一般认为，希腊数学家阿基米德在大约公元前 250 年发明了它。不过，也有可能，呃，古埃及人其实更早就在使用它。阿基米德或许是从埃及人那里了解到这种装置的，但我们并不确切知道。

阿基米德螺旋泵可不是用来组装家具之类东西的螺丝。想象一根比家具螺丝大得多的螺杆。和任何螺丝一样，它有螺纹，也就是环绕它盘旋的连续凸起。这道螺纹形成一条长长的螺旋，从螺杆的一端一直延伸到另一端，明白吗？这根长螺杆沿着一根长管的内部安装。这就是阿基米德螺旋泵。它用来把水从低处提升到较高的地方。使用时，把一端放入低处的水中，另一端斜着抬高；并不是竖直朝上，而是以更接近水平的倾角放置。然后转动它。水会进入管内，落在螺纹上。转动螺杆时，水就会被向上输送。

例如，这是一种从河流或湖泊中取水灌溉农田的有效方法，是一项对农业影响很大的技术。另外，有证据表明，在古代西班牙，人们使用阿基米德螺旋泵排出矿井中的水。除了西班牙的矿井之外，古代其他地方也用它排出船内的积水，甚至到今天，污水处理厂仍在使用它。

This was an effective way, for example, to get water from rivers or lakes to irrigate fields for crops, an impactful technology in agriculture. Also, there's evidence that in ancient Spain, they used the Archimedes screw to pump water out of mines. 请听历史课上的一段讲解。
有一种古代发明，叫阿基米德螺旋泵。一般认为，希腊数学家阿基米德在大约公元前 250 年发明了它。不过，也有可能，呃，古埃及人其实更早就在使用它。阿基米德或许是从埃及人那里了解到这种装置的，但我们并不确切知道。

speaking.answer: I try to get out into nature about two or three times a month, though it depends on my schedule. Usually I go to a large park near my house, which has a lake and walking trails. speaking.answer: I usually prefer relaxing, to be honest. After a busy week, I want to go somewhere peaceful, like a quiet lake or a forest path, and just enjoy it. I'll bring a book or a snack and sit for a while. Hiking up a steep mountain sounds exciting, but, um, it often leaves me too exhausted to enjoy the view. That said, I don't hate challenges. A couple of years ago I did a long hike with my cousin, and I felt proud when we reached the top. But that's something I do once in a while. Most of the time I go to nature to recover my energy, so relaxing fits me better. It helps me return to my routine feeling fresh.

speaking.answer: Absolutely, I really agree with this. I've noticed that even simple activities like gardening in my backyard significantly boost my mood. content.post: Paul: Using social media for educational purposes offers the advantage of real-time feedback and communication. It allows students to interact with their instructors outside of regular class times.

writing.answer:
Social media can support education effectively, but it should supplement a structured course rather than become the course itself. Paul is right that these platforms enable rapid questions, feedback, and collaboration outside class. A teacher might post a recent article, ask students to verify its claims, and let quieter students contribute thoughtfully in writing.

Kelly's concerns about access and privacy are serious. Schools should never require personal public accounts or assume every student has a reliable phone and constant internet connection. Public comment threads can also expose students to advertising, data collection, and harassment that have nothing to do with learning.

The best solution is a school-managed social platform with limited data collection, clear conduct rules, and equivalent offline options. Teachers should use it for focused tasks with defined deadlines, not endless scrolling. Under those conditions, social media can extend classroom discussion and teach responsible online communication while keeping participation safe, purposeful, and fair.

reading.explanation: 1. 这里 'shifts' 表示变化，与 'reflecting' 搭配，指爵士乐反映了文化变迁，符合上下文讨论爵士乐对文化的影响。 2. 'culture' 是名词，指文化，与前面的 'shifts' 构成 'cultural shifts'（文化变化），解释爵士乐所反映的社会背景。 3. 'employed' 是动词过去式，意为使用或采用，表示爵士乐采用了创新技术，与 'innovative techniques' 自然搭配。 4. 'techniques' 是名词，指技术或方法，形容词 'innovative' 修饰它，描述爵士乐的创新手法。 5. 'improvisation' 是名词，即兴创作，是爵士乐的核心特征，这里举例说明它如何挑战传统惯例。 6. 'challenged' 是动词过去式，表示挑战，指即兴创作等技巧挑战了传统音乐惯例，推动爵士乐发展。 7. 'musical' 是形容词，修饰 'conventions'，表示音乐的惯例，与上下文爵士乐主题一致，使表达更准确。 8. 'allowing' 是现在分词，表示允许或使能够，连接句子，说明挑战惯例的结果是使音乐家能表达个性。 9. 'to' 是不定式符号，与 'allowing' 构成 'allow sb to do sth' 固定搭配，表示允许做某事，语法上必须使用。 10. 'their' 是物主代词，指代 'musicians'，表示他们的个性，使表达具体并符合上下文指代。
reading.translation: 二十世纪初美国爵士乐的发展代表重大文化里程碑。源于新奥尔良的非裔美国人社区，爵士融合蓝调、拉格泰姆与欧洲古典音乐元素。反映文化变迁，爵士运用即兴等创新技巧挑战传统音乐惯例，使音乐家能表达个性。路易斯·阿姆斯特朗与艾拉·菲茨杰拉德等人物普及了爵士，在推进其风格创新中起关键作用。该类型影响扩展到全球，塑造各种音乐形式并激励新一代艺术家。

reading.translation: 古罗马社会是复杂的等级体系，具有鲜明的阶级制度。顶端是贵族——掌握多数政治权力的精英贵族家庭。多数人口特权、影响与权利有限，被称为平民。尽管人数更多，平民在共和国早期很大程度上被排除在正式政治决策之外。不过随着时间推移，他们争取并逐渐获得更多特权，例如担任公职的能力。

reading.title: Wilson Gym swimming pool maintenance
reading.prompt: Which of the following can be inferred about the Wilson Gym swimming pool?
reading.promptZh: 关于 Wilson 体育馆泳池，可以推断出下列哪一项？
reading.passage:
During the week of December 28–January 3, the swimming pool at Wilson Gym will be closed for maintenance.

While the pool closes annually for a week of maintenance, this year's closure will bring a significant change: a transition from the current chlorinated sanitation system to a saltwater-based system. Saltwater systems generate chlorine naturally from dissolved salt, creating a more comfortable swimming experience. Many swimmers find the water less irritating to their skin, eyes, and hair because the chlorine levels stay more consistent. Saltwater systems also eliminate the strong chemical smell associated with manually added chlorine.

The closure is timed to occur during winter break when many students are away. However, those remaining on campus who wish to swim during that week will have access to the pool at the YWCA on Biltmore St.

To use that pool, simply show your student ID at the front desk.

reading.title: The Rise of Circulating Libraries in England
reading.prompt: The passage indicates each of the following about circulating libraries EXCEPT:
reading.promptZh: 关于流通图书馆，文章提到了下列各项，除了：
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Circulating libraries emerged in eighteenth-century England as commercial institutions that transformed patterns of reading long before the rise of publicly funded libraries. Typically operated by booksellers or entrepreneurs, they relied on subscription fees that allowed members-predominantly middle-class women, but also clerks, tradespeople, and provincial professionals-to borrow popular fiction, travel narratives, and conduct literature. Their success reflected both the expansion of print culture and the growing popularity of leisure reading. As distributors of novels that were often viewed as frivolous or sensational, circulating libraries stoked anxieties about the effects of reading, especially on young women.

Paragraph 2
Some historians, such as David Allan, argue that circulating libraries played a democratizing role by widening access to books beyond elite circles at a time when books were expensive to buy. Others, including Jan Fergus, emphasize their commercial logic, contending that they reinforced existing social hierarchies by catering primarily to those who could afford subscriptions. A further line of scholarship questions whether these libraries should be viewed as precursors to the nineteenth-century nonprofit public library movement or as fundamentally distinct institutions shaped by consumer capitalism.

Paragraph 3
Despite these disagreements, circulating libraries undeniably reshaped England's literary marketplace, mediating between print production and everyday reading practices in ways that significantly affected how and what people read.

reading.translation:
关于流通图书馆，文章提到了下列各项，除了：

流通图书馆出现于十八世纪的英格兰，是在公共资助图书馆兴起之前就改变了阅读模式的商业机构。它们通常由书商或企业家经营，依靠订阅费运作，使会员——主要是中产妇女，也包括职员、商贩和外省专业人士——能够借阅流行小说、旅行叙事和品行读物。它们的成功既反映了印刷文化的扩张，也反映了休闲阅读的日益流行。作为常被看作轻浮或煽情的小说的传播者，流通图书馆加剧了人们对阅读影响的焦虑，尤其是对年轻女性的焦虑。
一些历史学家，如戴维·艾伦（David Allan），认为流通图书馆通过在书籍昂贵、难以购买的时代把获取书籍的机会扩大到精英圈子之外，发挥了民主化的作用。另一些人，包括简·弗格斯（Jan Fergus），则强调其商业逻辑，主张它们主要通过服务付得起订阅费的人来巩固既有社会等级。还有一派研究追问：这些图书馆究竟应被视为十九世纪非营利公共图书馆运动的先驱，还是由消费资本主义塑造的根本不同的机构。
尽管存在这些分歧，流通图书馆无可否认地重塑了英格兰的文学市场，在印刷生产与日常阅读实践之间起中介作用，并显著影响了人们如何阅读以及阅读什么。

reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
While quilting has historically been categorized as domestic labor, some quilts-bedcovers often made of pieces of fabric stitched together-cannot be adequately understood as mere works of household craft. For example, the quilts created by African American women from Gee's Bend, Alabama should be regarded as works of art, displaying intentional design, cultural expression, and aesthetic innovation that extend far beyond the boundaries of functional craft.

Paragraph 2
The Gee's Bend tradition demonstrates how a utilitarian form can evolve into a powerful artistic language. The quilters' bold improvisation, asymmetry, and inventive use of color parallel the visual strategies of modernist painters, yet they emerged independently from a rural, community-based practice rooted in everyday experience.

Paragraph 3
These quilts also operate as visual narratives. Each piece reflects personal history, collective memory, and the resourcefulness of women who transformed fabric scraps into compositions of striking emotional depth. reading.translation:

虽然绗缝长期以来被归入家务劳动，但有些被子——通常由布片缝合而成的床罩——不能仅仅被理解为家庭手工艺品。例如，美国亚拉巴马州吉斯本德的非裔美国妇女制作的被子应被视为艺术作品，它们展现出有意识的设计、文化表达和审美创新，远远超出了实用工艺的界限。
吉斯本德的传统表明，一种实用形式可以演变为强有力的艺术语言。这些绗缝者大胆的即兴、不对称和富于发明的用色，与现代主义画家的视觉策略相平行，但它们却独立地产生于扎根日常经验的乡村社区实践。
这些被子也充当视觉叙事。每一件作品都反映出个人历史、集体记忆，以及把碎布转化为具有惊人情感深度的构图的机智。它们的作品挑战了长期把“纯艺术”与“工艺”分开的等级秩序，而这种区分往往由性别、种族和阶级塑造。承认这些被子是艺术，就是承认这一历史上被低估的传统中所蕴含的创作严谨性。这并不是说被子不是工艺；相反，这些被子表明工艺与艺术可以共存于同一件物品之中。

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: The formation of river deltas is a geographical process that illustrates the dynamic interaction between land and water. When a river reaches a body of water, such as an [1] oc___ or [2] s__, it [3] sl___ down, [4] depos_____ the [5] mate_____ it has [6] car____ from [7] upst____. Gradually, [8] t__ sediments [9] accum_____ to [10] cre___ deltas, which are fertile landforms that extend into the water. Deltas not only support diverse ecosystems but also provide rich agricultural land.

reading.answer:
1. ean → ocean
2. ea → sea
3. ows → slows
4. iting → depositing
5. rials → materials
6. ried → carried
7. ream → upstream
8. he → the
9. ulate → accumulate
10. ate → create
reading.explanation: 1. 因为前面是'an'，表示元音开头，且上下文提到'a body of water'，所以填表示海洋的'ocean'。 2. 与'ocean'并列，用'or'连接，表示另一种水域如海，所以填'sea'。 3. 动词短语'slow down'表示减速，符合河流到达水域时速度变慢的语境。 4. 现在分词作伴随状语，描述河流在减速时沉积材料的动作。 5. 名词，指河流从上游携带的物质，与'depositing'搭配，表示沉积的对象。 6. 现在完成时'has carried'，表示河流已经携带了这些材料，强调对现在的影响。 7. 介词'from'后接地点，指材料来自上游，与前文'from upstream'一致。 8. 定冠词'the'特指前文提到的沉积物，表示这些特定的沉积物。 9. 不定式'to accumulate'表示目的，沉积物积累以形成三角洲，符合句子结构。 10. 不定式'to create'表示目的，沉积物积累后创造三角洲，与前文'accumulation'呼应。
reading.translation: 河流三角洲的形成是说明陆地与水动态互动的地理过程。当河流到达海洋或海等水体时，流速减慢，沉积从上游携带的物质。逐渐地，沉积物堆积形成延伸入水的肥沃地貌——三角洲。三角洲不仅支持多样生态系统，也提供肥沃农地。

reading.title: Female Education in Eighteenth-Century England
reading.prompt: The word "aspiration" in the passage is closest in meaning to
reading.promptZh: 文中单词 aspiration 的意思最接近
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Education for girls in eighteenth-century England reflected entrenched assumptions about gender, social hierarchy, and learning. Dominant attitudes held that women required only limited instruction-sufficient to cultivate virtue, domestic skills, and refinement. Intellectual aspiration was generally regarded as unhealthy for women.

Paragraph 2
Access to schooling reflected class distinctions. Girls from elite families often attended small boarding schools with curricula that emphasized so-called accomplishments such as music, drawing, needlework, modern languages, and basic literacy, subjects intended to enhance sociability rather than foster intellectual development. Middle-class girls typically received home-schooling, combining reading and writing with domestic training. For working-class girls, opportunities were minimal; many acquired only rudimentary literacy or vocational skills, while others received no schooling at all.

Paragraph 3
Yet the period also saw the emergence of challenges to the prevailing norms. The philosophers Mary Astell and Mary Wollstonecraft contended that women possessed the same rational faculties as men and merited an education oriented toward intellectual development rather than ornamental refinement. Their critiques exposed tensions within eighteenth-century Enlightenment discourse, which celebrated reason while nonetheless denying its cultivation to women. Although these critiques did not immediately transform educational practice, they articulated a philosophical foundation that would inspire later feminist thinkers and broaden conceptions of women's intellectual and civic potential.

reading.translation:
文中单词 aspiration 的意思最接近

十八世纪英格兰的女孩教育反映了关于性别、社会等级和学习的根深蒂固的假定。主流态度认为，女性只需要有限的教导——足以培养德行、家务技能和文雅即可。知识上的抱负通常被视为对女性有害。
入学机会反映出阶级差异。精英家庭的女孩往往就读小型寄宿学校，课程强调所谓才艺，如音乐、绘画、针线、现代语言和基本读写，这些科目意在增进社交能力而非促进心智发展。中产女孩通常在家接受教育，把读写与家务训练结合起来。劳工阶级女孩的机会极少；许多人只获得粗浅读写或职业技能，另一些人则完全没有上学。
不过这一时期也出现了对主流规范的挑战。哲学家玛丽·阿斯特尔（Mary Astell）和玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特（Mary Wollstonecraft）主张，女性拥有与男性相同的理性能力，理应接受面向心智发展而非装饰性文雅的教育。她们的批判揭示了十八世纪启蒙话语内部的张力：它颂扬理性，却拒绝让女性培养理性。尽管这些批判并未立即改变教育实践，它们却阐明了一个将启发后世女权思想家、并拓宽人们对女性智识与公民潜能之理解的哲学基础。

reading.title: Female Education in Eighteenth-Century England
reading.prompt: According to the passage, Mary Astell and Mary Wollstonecraft based their arguments challenging the prevailing norms on which of the following claims?
reading.promptZh: 根据文章，玛丽·阿斯特尔和玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特挑战主流规范的论据基于下列哪一主张？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Education for girls in eighteenth-century England reflected entrenched assumptions about gender, social hierarchy, and learning. Dominant attitudes held that women required only limited instruction-sufficient to cultivate virtue, domestic skills, and refinement. Intellectual aspiration was generally regarded as unhealthy for women.

Paragraph 2
Access to schooling reflected class distinctions. Girls from elite families often attended small boarding schools with curricula that emphasized so-called accomplishments such as music, drawing, needlework, modern languages, and basic literacy, subjects intended to enhance sociability rather than foster intellectual development. Middle-class girls typically received home-schooling, combining reading and writing with domestic training. For working-class girls, opportunities were minimal; many acquired only rudimentary literacy or vocational skills, while others received no schooling at all.

Paragraph 3
Yet the period also saw the emergence of challenges to the prevailing norms. The philosophers Mary Astell and Mary Wollstonecraft contended that women possessed the same rational faculties as men and merited an education oriented toward intellectual development rather than ornamental refinement. Their critiques exposed tensions within eighteenth-century Enlightenment discourse, which celebrated reason while nonetheless denying its cultivation to women. Although these critiques did not immediately transform educational practice, they articulated a philosophical foundation that would inspire later feminist thinkers and broaden conceptions of women's intellectual and civic potential.

reading.translation:
根据文章，玛丽·阿斯特尔和玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特挑战主流规范的论据基于下列哪一主张？

十八世纪英格兰的女孩教育反映了关于性别、社会等级和学习的根深蒂固的假定。主流态度认为，女性只需要有限的教导——足以培养德行、家务技能和文雅即可。知识上的抱负通常被视为对女性有害。
入学机会反映出阶级差异。精英家庭的女孩往往就读小型寄宿学校，课程强调所谓才艺，如音乐、绘画、针线、现代语言和基本读写，这些科目意在增进社交能力而非促进心智发展。中产女孩通常在家接受教育，把读写与家务训练结合起来。劳工阶级女孩的机会极少；许多人只获得粗浅读写或职业技能，另一些人则完全没有上学。
不过这一时期也出现了对主流规范的挑战。哲学家玛丽·阿斯特尔（Mary Astell）和玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特（Mary Wollstonecraft）主张，女性拥有与男性相同的理性能力，理应接受面向心智发展而非装饰性文雅的教育。她们的批判揭示了十八世纪启蒙话语内部的张力：它颂扬理性，却拒绝让女性培养理性。尽管这些批判并未立即改变教育实践，它们却阐明了一个将启发后世女权思想家、并拓宽人们对女性智识与公民潜能之理解的哲学基础。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Hey, do you still work on cars for fun? I know someone who could use some advice.
Woman: I sure do.
Man: My roommate, Max, wants to buy an old car and fix it up over summer break. His parents have a big backyard, so there's plenty of space to work on it.
Woman: It can be really fun and really time-consuming. Does Max have the time and skill to do it?
Man: The time? Yes. But let's just say he has a lot to learn. I'm sure he'd be willing to pay you for your expertise.
Woman: Well, maybe I could go with him to look at the car first. Then we could take it from there.

男：嘿，你还会把修车当作爱好吗？我认识一个人，他需要一些建议。

男：我室友Max想买一辆旧车，在暑假把它修好。他父母家有个很大的后院，有充足空间可以干活。
女：这会很有趣，但也非常耗时间。Max有足够的时间和技术吗？

女：嗯，也许我可以先陪他去看看那辆车，然后再决定下一步。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an ecology class.
Soil fertility doesn't just depend on minerals or fertilizers. It also depends on microbes, especially bacteria that live around plant roots. These microbes break down organic matter and release nutrients that plants can absorb. But for these processes to work well, bacteria often need to act together, not just individually. One way they coordinate their behavior is through quorum sensing, figuring out if there's enough of them around. Bacteria release and detect chemical signals. Think of it like leaving notes on a shared bulletin board. One note doesn't make much difference, but when enough notes accumulate, everyone in the community notices. That's when the group, the bacteria, shift from working alone to coordinated action. An example of this kind of coordination is the formation of biofilms—sticky communities that cling to soil particles or root surfaces. Building biofilms benefits both the microbes and plants, because it improves the microbes' ability to capture and retain nutrients. But building a biofilm is expensive for the bacteria in energy terms, so it's beneficial for them to wait until there's a large enough group before committing. If they start too early, there may not be enough cells to sustain the structure, which would make it a waste of energy. Quorum sensing helps them decide when it's worth pooling effort. And plants can actually influence this system. Roots release chemical compounds that magnify microbial signals. This helps recruit the helpful microbes that the plants need.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段生态学课上的讲解。
土壤肥力不只取决于矿物质或肥料，还取决于微生物，尤其是生活在植物根系周围的细菌。这些微生物分解有机物，释放植物能吸收的养分。但要让这些过程顺利进行，细菌往往需要协同行动，而不是各自为战。它们协调行为的一种方式是群体感应，也就是判断周围同类是否足够多。细菌释放并检测化学信号。可以想象成在共享布告栏上留言。一条留言没什么作用，但当留言足够多时，社区里的每个成员都会注意到。那时，细菌群体就会从单打独斗转向协同行动。这种协同的一个例子是生物膜的形成，也就是附着在土壤颗粒或根表的黏性群落。形成生物膜对微生物和植物都有利，因为它提高了微生物捕获和保存养分的能力。但形成生物膜对细菌来说能耗很高，所以最好等到群体足够大再投入。如果开始得太早，细胞数量可能不足以维持结构，就会浪费能量。群体感应帮助它们判断何时值得合力。而植物其实也能影响这套系统。根系会释放化学物质来放大微生物信号，从而招募植物需要的有益微生物。

Soil fertility doesn't just depend on minerals or fertilizers. It also depends on microbes, especially bacteria that live around plant roots. listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk on an architecture podcast.
The great pyramids in Egypt were basically built by piling one stone on top of another. Many of the stones used to build them contain huge numbers of one specific type of fossil shell. These shells resemble the size and shape of small coins, and the scientific name of the shells reflects this. The organisms that form these shells are called nummulites. That's a word with the same root as the word numismatics, which is the study of money. And coins are money, right? Okay, so considering that these shells, while small, are still large enough to collect in your hand, it may come as a surprise that they were created by a unicellular organism. A creature that consisted of just one single huge cell, not a multicellular organism like clams or oysters. Amazing, right? Large numbers of these shell-making organisms once lived on a tropical seafloor millions of years ago in what's now Egypt. Over time, huge numbers of these shells were buried beneath many additional layers. The weight of the overlying layers compacted the limey sediment closer together until it turned into a solid rock known as limestone. But limestone that was rich in nummulites wasn't suitable for construction in all sections of the pyramids, so other types of stone had to be quarried as well. Okay, next up. Let's look at the pyramid structure and why different kinds of stone were used for different parts.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段建筑播客。
埃及的大金字塔基本上是把石头一层层垒起来建成的。用来建造它们的许多石头里，含有大量某一种特定的化石贝壳。这些贝壳的大小和形状像小硬币，其学名也反映了这一点。形成这些贝壳的生物叫货币虫。这个词和 numismatics（钱币学）同源，而钱币就是钱，对吧？这些贝壳虽然小，却大到能放在手里把玩，所以它们其实由单细胞生物创造，可能让人意外。那种生物只有一个大细胞，不是蛤蜊或牡蛎那样的多细胞生物。很神奇吧？数不清的造壳生物曾生活在数百万年前、如今埃及一带的热带海底。随着时间推移，大量贝壳被埋在更多沉积层之下。上覆地层的重量把灰质沉积压实，最终变成称为石灰岩的坚硬岩石。但富含货币虫的石灰岩并不适合金字塔所有部位的建造，因此还需要开采其他类型的石头。好，接下来我们看看金字塔的结构，以及为什么不同部位要用不同石材。

listening.translation: 说话人接下来最可能讨论什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk on an architecture podcast.
The great pyramids in Egypt were basically built by piling one stone on top of another. Many of the stones used to build them contain huge numbers of one specific type of fossil shell. These shells resemble the size and shape of small coins, and the scientific name of the shells reflects this. The organisms that form these shells are called nummulites. That's a word with the same root as the word numismatics, which is the study of money. And coins are money, right? Okay, so considering that these shells, while small, are still large enough to collect in your hand, it may come as a surprise that they were created by a unicellular organism. A creature that consisted of just one single huge cell, not a multicellular organism like clams or oysters. Amazing, right? Large numbers of these shell-making organisms once lived on a tropical seafloor millions of years ago in what's now Egypt. Over time, huge numbers of these shells were buried beneath many additional layers. The weight of the overlying layers compacted the limey sediment closer together until it turned into a solid rock known as limestone. But limestone that was rich in nummulites wasn't suitable for construction in all sections of the pyramids, so other types of stone had to be quarried as well. Okay, next up. Let's look at the pyramid structure and why different kinds of stone were used for different parts.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段建筑播客。
埃及的大金字塔基本上是把石头一层层垒起来建成的。用来建造它们的许多石头里，含有大量某一种特定的化石贝壳。这些贝壳的大小和形状像小硬币，其学名也反映了这一点。形成这些贝壳的生物叫货币虫。这个词和 numismatics（钱币学）同源，而钱币就是钱，对吧？这些贝壳虽然小，却大到能放在手里把玩，所以它们其实由单细胞生物创造，可能让人意外。那种生物只有一个大细胞，不是蛤蜊或牡蛎那样的多细胞生物。很神奇吧？数不清的造壳生物曾生活在数百万年前、如今埃及一带的热带海底。随着时间推移，大量贝壳被埋在更多沉积层之下。上覆地层的重量把灰质沉积压实，最终变成称为石灰岩的坚硬岩石。但富含货币虫的石灰岩并不适合金字塔所有部位的建造，因此还需要开采其他类型的石头。好，接下来我们看看金字塔的结构，以及为什么不同部位要用不同石材。

listening.translation: 这段讲解主要讲什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music appreciation class.
Have you ever wondered why music has such a strong emotional impact on us? Sometimes it comes from the way our brains respond to what's called dissonance. Dissonance occurs when two or more notes clash. They sound together in a way that creates tension or instability. Imagine hitting two piano keys that are right next to each other. It creates a sound that feels unresolved. Why does this matter? Well, music thrives on the tension between opposites. So dissonance is what creates a sense of unease that begs the solution, to move to harmony. And when that resolution comes, say those two notes resolve into a harmonious chord, it feels like a breath of fresh air. This combination of tension and release forms the emotional push and pull of music. Here's something you might not know though. The use of dissonance hasn't always been welcome. There were long periods in European history during which dissonance in music was considered sinful by the religious authorities at the time. But then, in the 1700s, the German composer Johann Sebastian Bach came along. Bach started using dissonance more dynamically, and it became central to compositions. And today, modern genres like jazz and experimental music rely heavily on the unique emotions dissonance creates. Let's listen to some modern music.

请听一段音乐欣赏课上的讲解。
你是否想过，为什么音乐对我们的情绪影响如此强烈？有时这来自大脑对所谓不协和音的反应。当两个或多个音符冲突时，就产生不协和。它们同时响起，制造出紧张或不稳定感。想象一下，同时按下相邻的两个钢琴键。听起来悬而未决。这为什么重要？因为音乐恰恰建立在对立面的张力之上。不协和音制造出一种不安，逼着我们寻找解决，也就是走向和谐。当解决到来，比如那两个音符落到一个和谐的和弦上，会让人松一口气。紧张与释放的组合，构成了音乐的情绪推拉。不过有一点你可能不知道。不协和音的使用并不一直受欢迎。欧洲历史上有很长时期，宗教当局认为音乐中的不协和是罪恶的。到了十八世纪，德国作曲家约翰·塞巴斯蒂安·巴赫出现。巴赫更动态地使用不协和音，它于是成为作曲的核心。今天，爵士和实验音乐等现代风格，都重度依赖不协和音创造的独特情绪。我们来听一些现代音乐。

listening.translation: 当不协和解决为和谐时会怎样？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music appreciation class.
Have you ever wondered why music has such a strong emotional impact on us? Sometimes it comes from the way our brains respond to what's called dissonance. Dissonance occurs when two or more notes clash. They sound together in a way that creates tension or instability. Imagine hitting two piano keys that are right next to each other. It creates a sound that feels unresolved. Why does this matter? Well, music thrives on the tension between opposites. So dissonance is what creates a sense of unease that begs the solution, to move to harmony. And when that resolution comes, say those two notes resolve into a harmonious chord, it feels like a breath of fresh air. This combination of tension and release forms the emotional push and pull of music. Here's something you might not know though. The use of dissonance hasn't always been welcome. There were long periods in European history during which dissonance in music was considered sinful by the religious authorities at the time. But then, in the 1700s, the German composer Johann Sebastian Bach came along. Bach started using dissonance more dynamically, and it became central to compositions. And today, modern genres like jazz and experimental music rely heavily on the unique emotions dissonance creates. Let's listen to some modern music.

listening.translation: 说话人主要讨论什么？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a film class.
As you know, Hollywood California is associated with movies. Early Hollywood, through the 1920s or so, was the period of silent films, with no recorded dialogue. Maybe you've heard of Charlie Chaplin, a famous silent film star. He was prolific early in the century. Movies remained silent until the first full-length sound film with spoken dialogue throughout was called The Jazz Singer. But that, The Jazz Singer, came out later, not till 1927. One important filmmaker's career spanned the silent film era and later. Her name was Dorothy Arzner. Arzner's career was unusual for a woman at that time. I can think of maybe one other female director who had a long Hollywood career in those days. Well, Dorothy Arzner started out by typing scripts and then editing film. Then, in 1922, she had an opportunity to edit and direct for a silent film called Blood and Sand. It irritates me that she was not credited as an editor or director for Blood and Sand. It's unfair. She made decisions that saved the movie studio thousands of dollars. She deserved acknowledgment. From there, Arzner made about 20 films and was credited for her work. In fact, she was the first woman to direct a sound film. Many of her films deal with, shall we say, unconventional romance stories, unexpected characters meeting, falling in love, getting married. Arzner's films introduced several women actors who would go on to become hugely successful in comedies and dramas themselves.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段电影课上的讲解。
你们都知道，加州好莱坞与电影紧密相连。到二十世纪二十年代前后，早期好莱坞是默片时期，没有录制对白。你们可能听说过查理·卓别林，著名的默片明星。他在本世纪初非常高产。电影一直保持无声，直到第一部从头到尾都有对白的全长有声片《爵士歌手》问世。不过《爵士歌手》出现得更晚，要到一九二七年。有一位重要电影人的生涯横跨默片与后来的有声时代。她就是多萝西·阿兹纳。以当时女性而言，阿兹纳的职业生涯很不寻常。那个年代在好莱坞拥有漫长导演生涯的女性，我能想到的大概只有一位。多萝西·阿兹纳从打字剧本起步，后来剪辑影片。一九二二年，她有机会为默片《血与沙》担任剪辑和导演。让我恼火的是，《血与沙》没有给她剪辑或导演署名。这不公平。她做出的决定为电影公司省下数千美元。她应得认可。此后阿兹纳拍了大约二十部电影，并获得署名。事实上，她是第一位执导有声电影的女性。她的许多影片处理的是，怎么说呢，非传统的爱情故事，意想不到的角色相遇、相爱、结婚。阿兹纳的影片启用了多位女演员，她们后来在喜剧和正剧中都大获成功。

listening.translation: 对《血与沙》，说话人持什么态度？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a film class.
As you know, Hollywood California is associated with movies. Early Hollywood, through the 1920s or so, was the period of silent films, with no recorded dialogue. Maybe you've heard of Charlie Chaplin, a famous silent film star. He was prolific early in the century. Movies remained silent until the first full-length sound film with spoken dialogue throughout was called The Jazz Singer. But that, The Jazz Singer, came out later, not till 1927. One important filmmaker's career spanned the silent film era and later. Her name was Dorothy Arzner. Arzner's career was unusual for a woman at that time. I can think of maybe one other female director who had a long Hollywood career in those days. Well, Dorothy Arzner started out by typing scripts and then editing film. Then, in 1922, she had an opportunity to edit and direct for a silent film called Blood and Sand. It irritates me that she was not credited as an editor or director for Blood and Sand. It's unfair. She made decisions that saved the movie studio thousands of dollars. She deserved acknowledgment. From there, Arzner made about 20 films and was credited for her work. In fact, she was the first woman to direct a sound film. Many of her films deal with, shall we say, unconventional romance stories, unexpected characters meeting, falling in love, getting married. Arzner's films introduced several women actors who would go on to become hugely successful in comedies and dramas themselves.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段电影课上的讲解。
你们都知道，加州好莱坞与电影紧密相连。到二十世纪二十年代前后，早期好莱坞是默片时期，没有录制对白。你们可能听说过查理·卓别林，著名的默片明星。他在本世纪初非常高产。电影一直保持无声，直到第一部从头到尾都有对白的全长有声片《爵士歌手》问世。不过《爵士歌手》出现得更晚，要到一九二七年。有一位重要电影人的生涯横跨默片与后来的有声时代。她就是多萝西·阿兹纳。以当时女性而言，阿兹纳的职业生涯很不寻常。那个年代在好莱坞拥有漫长导演生涯的女性，我能想到的大概只有一位。多萝西·阿兹纳从打字剧本起步，后来剪辑影片。一九二二年，她有机会为默片《血与沙》担任剪辑和导演。让我恼火的是，《血与沙》没有给她剪辑或导演署名。这不公平。她做出的决定为电影公司省下数千美元。她应得认可。此后阿兹纳拍了大约二十部电影，并获得署名。事实上，她是第一位执导有声电影的女性。她的许多影片处理的是，怎么说呢，非传统的爱情故事，意想不到的角色相遇、相爱、结婚。阿兹纳的影片启用了多位女演员，她们后来在喜剧和正剧中都大获成功。

speaking.answer: Yes, I have a few small plants on my balcony, mostly herbs like basil and mint, and one little cactus. I water them every morning, and, um, once a week I check the soil and trim the leaves. It probably takes about ten minutes a day, so it's not a big commitment. I started last spring, when I wanted something green in my apartment, and honestly it turned out to be really relaxing. I love picking fresh basil for my pasta. I plan to add tomatoes next year. The cactus is my favorite, because it's tough and needs almost no attention at all. Of course, I forgot to water the mint once during a busy week, and it almost died. Now I keep a reminder on my phone, and I've become much more responsible with them.

content.promptText: Thank you. What kinds of plants or gardens have you seen or heard about that you found interesting or appealing? Describe them and talk about why you found them interesting or appealing.

speaking.answer: One garden I remember is a Japanese garden I visited with my family a few years ago. It had stones, a little pond, and carefully shaped trees, and, uh, everything felt perfectly calm. There was almost no noise, even though many visitors were walking around. I was amazed by how every small detail had a purpose, like the way the water moved through the stones. I also read about rooftop gardens in big cities, where people grow vegetables on tall buildings. I find those interesting too, because they bring nature into crowded places. What appeals to me most is that gardens can give peace to people, and that they make a place feel alive, no matter how small the space is.

content.promptText: I see. What challenges do you think people face when trying to grow plants or maintain a garden?

speaking.answer: I think the biggest challenge is time. Plants need regular care, and, uh, many people are too busy to water them or notice problems. Another challenge is knowledge. Different plants need different amounts of sun and water, and beginners often give too much or too little. I mean, I've killed a few plants that way myself. Weather can be a problem too. A sudden frost or a hot dry summer can ruin months of work. Then there are pests, like insects eating the leaves, which can be frustrating. Space is also an issue for people living in apartments. Still, honestly, I believe these problems can be solved with patience, a little research, and choosing easy plants like herbs at the beginning.

speaking.answer: Absolutely, I strongly agree with that viewpoint. In my own experience, spending time with plants, even just briefly, has a real calming effect on me. You know, there's something almost meditative about the repetitive tasks like pruning or watering; it forces you to slow down and just be present. Hmm, I think it also gives you a genuine sense of accomplishment when you see something you nurtured actually thrive and produce flowers or fruit. Another thing is that it gets you outdoors and away from screens, which honestly makes a huge difference in reducing daily stress. So, I definitely believe that even a small garden can significantly boost someone's emotional wellbeing.

On one hand, this means we can access diverse viewpoints and stay updated instantly, which can broaden our understanding of the world. On the other hand, not all information is accurate, leading to confusion and, sometimes, false beliefs, which may deepen divisions among people. What do you think? Is the proliferation of online news sources making people more informed or contributing to misinformation and polarization?
content.post: Paul: In my opinion, it’s up to individuals to learn how to navigate the sea of information better. We must learn to identify credible sources and ignore the rest. This skill is essential in today’s world. If we learn how to distinguish between what’s credible and what’s sensational and choose the credible sources, we eliminate the market for clickbait.

writing.answer:
The expansion of online news can make people better informed, but only when readers and platforms take verification seriously. Paul is right that media literacy matters. Before sharing a dramatic claim, readers should check the original evidence, compare several reputable outlets, and distinguish reporting from opinion. These habits make access to many perspectives genuinely valuable.

Claire's concern is equally important because online platforms profit from attention. An inaccurate headline that provokes anger may travel much farther than a careful correction, and recommendation systems can repeatedly show users material that confirms existing beliefs. Individual judgment alone cannot fully overcome that design.

Schools should teach source evaluation through real examples, while platforms should label altered media, disclose why content is recommended, and reduce rewards for demonstrably false stories. With those safeguards, abundant online news can broaden public understanding. Without them, the same abundance creates confusion and pushes groups into separate information worlds, deepening misinformation and polarization.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: Philosophy investigates the nature of reality, existence, and knowledge through critical thinking and reasoning. It [1] expl____ fundamental [2] ques_____ about [3] t__ human [4] exper_____, ethics, [5] a__ the [6] mi__. Philosophers [7] dev____ theories [8] t_ better [9] under_____ the [10] wo___ and our place in it. This discipline challenges individuals to reflect deeply on their beliefs and assumptions, fostering intellectual growth and enlightenment. Contemporary philosophical branches include bioethics, philosophy of mind, and environmental philosophy, addressing modern challenges such as artificial intelligence consciousness, genetic engineering ethics, and humanity’s relationship with nature.

reading.answer:
1. ores → explores
2. tions → questions
3. he → the
4. ience → experience
5. nd → and
6. nd → mind
7. elop → develop
8. o → to
9. stand → understand
10. rld → world
reading.explanation: 1. 此处需要一个动词作谓语，与后文宾语 'questions' 搭配，'explores' 表示 '探索'，符合哲学研究基本问题的语境。 2. 此处需要一个名词作宾语，且与形容词 'fundamental' (基本的) 搭配，'questions' (问题) 是哲学探讨的核心对象。 3. 此处需要定冠词特指后文 'human experience' (人类经验) 这一哲学研究的具体领域。 4. 此处需要名词，与 'human' 搭配构成哲学的研究对象之一，'experience' (经验) 是哲学中的重要概念。 5. 此处需要连词，用于连接 'ethics' (伦理学) 和 'the mind' (心灵) 这两个并列的宾语。 6. 此处需要名词，与 'the' 搭配，'mind' (心灵/心智) 是哲学（如心灵哲学）研究的基本领域之一。 7. 此处需要动词原形，表示哲学家们的动作，'develop' (发展/提出) 理论是为了理解世界。 8. 此处需要不定式符号 'to'，构成 'to better understand' (为了更好理解) 的目的状语。 9. 此处需要动词原形，构成 'to better understand'，'understand' (理解) 是发展理论的目的。 10. 此处需要名词作宾语，'the world' (世界) 与后文 'our place in it' (我们其中的位置) 形成紧密的逻辑关联。
reading.translation: 哲学通过批判思维与推理探究现实、存在与知识的本质。它探索关于人类体验、伦理与心灵的基本问题。哲学家发展理论以更好理解世界及我们在其中的位置。这一学科挑战个体深刻反思其信念与假设，培养智识成长与启蒙。当代哲学分支包括生命伦理、心灵哲学与环境哲学，应对人工智能意识、基因工程伦理以及人类与自然关系等现代挑战。

Warm colors, like red and orange, can suggest energy or passion. Cool tones, like blue and green, can evoke calm or melancholy. Through deliberate choices, artists shape the visual and emotional impact of their work.

reading.answer:
1. cit → elicit
2. ods → moods
3. fully → carefully
4. mentary → complementary
5. asting → contrasting
6. ey → they
7. hten → heighten
8. act → impact
9. ate → create
10. sitions → compositions
reading.explanation: 1. 前缀'eli'提示动词'elicit'，意为引发，与后文'moods'（情绪）搭配合理，表示引发特定情绪。 2. 与'specific'（具体的）搭配，指具体的情绪，故填'moods'。 3. 由'care'开头，表示仔细地，修饰动词'selecting'（选择），故填副词'carefully'。 4. 颜色理论中，'complementary'（互补的）与'contrasting'（对比的）并列，指互补色，故填此词。 5. 与'complementary'并列，指对比色，故填'contrasting'。 6. 句子主语需要代词，'they'指代前文的'Artists'（艺术家），故填此词。 7. 前缀'heig'提示动词'heighten'（增强），与'visual impact'（视觉冲击力）搭配，表示增强视觉影响。 8. 与'visual'（视觉的）搭配，指视觉冲击力，故填名词'impact'。 9. 与'dynamic compositions'（动态构图）搭配，表示创造，故填动词'create'。 10. 艺术术语，指构图，与'dynamic'（动态的）搭配，故填'compositions'。
reading.translation: 艺术中的色彩运用是传达情绪、创造深度并引导观者注意力的强大工具。艺术家用色彩理论以引发特定氛围的方式组合色调。通过精心选择互补或对比色，他们可增强视觉冲击并创造动态构图。红与橙等暖色可暗示能量或激情。蓝与绿等冷色可唤起平静或忧郁。通过刻意选择，艺术家塑造作品的视觉与情感影响。

reading.title: GHOSTLY WHISPERS IN LIBRARY
reading.prompt: What is the main topic of the article?
reading.promptZh: 文章的主要话题是什么？
reading.passage:
GHOSTLY WHISPERS IN LIBRARY
Greenfield University's historic library has become the center of spooky rumors after students reported whispers and flickering lights during late-night study sessions. "I swear I saw a ghostly figure," said senior Emma Li, who shared her experience on social media.
The mystery began when renovations uncovered a reading room that had been sealed since 1904. Paranormal clubs are planning a midnight investigation with cameras and audio recorders, while campus security insists the disturbances are due to "old wiring and drafts."
Still, the story has sparked excitement across campus. "It's creepy but funny," said freshman Noah Grant, who plans to livestream the ghost hunt. The library staff has embraced the buzz, adding a "Haunted History" display near the entrance featuring old photographs and letters.
Whether it's a ghost or just campus folklore, the rumors have turned the library into the most talked-about spot on campus this semester.

reading.translation:
关于第1段提到的“野牛（大型、类似牛的动物）、手印和抽象符号等图像”，可以推断出什么？

史前洞穴壁画既具有视觉冲击力，又充满神秘感，促使学者推断创作者的动机以及这些图像可能意味着什么。许多研究者认为，这些绘画是早期的交流和记忆保存形式，使史前人类能够记录经历或宣告自身的存在。野牛（大型、类似牛的动物）、手印和抽象符号等图像出现在不同大陆，表明人们有着记录生活与身份的共同冲动。
另一些学者强调可能的精神或仪式动机。许多绘画出现在洞穴深处、并非日常起居的空间。一些考古学家推测这些地点具有象征功能。图像可能与狩猎仪式、成年礼，或试图影响自然力量有关。拉斯科和肖维等遗址中常见的动物与狩猎场景，支持把艺术与信仰体系或集体仪式联系起来的解释。
第三种视角把洞穴艺术看作早期讲故事和教学的表达。这些图像可能具有教育功能，用来向较年轻的群体成员传递关于动物、地貌或社会规范的知识。综合来看，这些解释表明洞穴壁画未必只为单一目的而作，而是反映了交流、仪式与创造性表达的复杂混合。

reading.promptZh: 根据“第三种视角”，洞穴图像
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Prehistoric cave paintings are both visually powerful and mysterious, inviting scholars to infer what motivated their creators and what the images may have meant. Many researchers argue that these paintings served as an early form of communication and memory-keeping, allowing prehistoric people to record experiences or announce their presence. Images such as bison (large, ox-like animals), handprints, and abstract symbols appear across continents, suggesting shared impulses to document life and identity.

Paragraph 2
Other scholars emphasize possible spiritual or ritual motivations. Many paintings appear deep inside caves in spaces not used for daily living. Some archaeologists speculate that these locations had symbolic functions. The imagery may have been tied to hunting rituals, initiation practices, or attempts to influence natural forces. Paintings of animals and hunting scenes, common in sites like Lascaux and Chauvet, support interpretations that link art to belief systems or communal ceremonies.

Paragraph 3
A third perspective views cave art as an expression of early storytelling and teaching. The images may have had a pedagogical function, serving to convey knowledge about animals, landscapes, or social norms to younger group members. Together, these interpretations suggest that cave paintings may not have been created for a single purpose but reflected a complex blend of communication, ritual, and creative expression.

reading.translation:
根据“第三种视角”，洞穴图像

史前洞穴壁画既具有视觉冲击力，又充满神秘感，促使学者推断创作者的动机以及这些图像可能意味着什么。许多研究者认为，这些绘画是早期的交流和记忆保存形式，使史前人类能够记录经历或宣告自身的存在。野牛（大型、类似牛的动物）、手印和抽象符号等图像出现在不同大陆，表明人们有着记录生活与身份的共同冲动。
另一些学者强调可能的精神或仪式动机。许多绘画出现在洞穴深处、并非日常起居的空间。一些考古学家推测这些地点具有象征功能。图像可能与狩猎仪式、成年礼，或试图影响自然力量有关。拉斯科和肖维等遗址中常见的动物与狩猎场景，支持把艺术与信仰体系或集体仪式联系起来的解释。
第三种视角把洞穴艺术看作早期讲故事和教学的表达。这些图像可能具有教育功能，用来向较年轻的群体成员传递关于动物、地貌或社会规范的知识。综合来看，这些解释表明洞穴壁画未必只为单一目的而作，而是反映了交流、仪式与创造性表达的复杂混合。

reading.title: Kinship Ties
reading.prompt: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
reading.passage: In the prehistoric era, social organization was intricately linked to the prevailing environmental conditions, which dictated the migratory patterns and settlement choices of early human groups. These [1] commu______ often [2] deve_____ cohesive [3] un___ based [4] o_ kinship [5] ti__, establishing a [6] sim___ social [7] stru_____ that [8] facil______ cooperative [9] hun____ and [10] gath_____ of food. Leadership roles emerged naturally, typically assumed by individuals possessing superior survival skills or profound knowledge of the terrain. The distribution of resources, particularly food, was a critical factor, often determining the power dynamics within the group.

content.promptText: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
content.stimulusText: In the prehistoric era, social organization was intricately linked to the prevailing environmental conditions, which dictated the migratory patterns and settlement choices of early human groups. These [1] commu______ often [2] deve_____ cohesive [3] un___ based [4] o_ kinship [5] ti__, establishing a [6] sim___ social [7] stru_____ that [8] facil______ cooperative [9] hun____ and [10] gath_____ of food. Leadership roles emerged naturally, typically assumed by individuals possessing superior survival skills or profound knowledge of the terrain. The distribution of resources, particularly food, was a critical factor, often determining the power dynamics within the group.

reading.answer:
1. nities → communities
2. loped → developed
3. its → units
4. n → on
5. es → ties
6. ple → simple
7. cture → structure
8. itated → facilitated
9. ting → hunting
10. ering → gathering
reading.explanation: 1. 指代前文的'early human groups'，表示这些社区（communities）是社交组织的基本单位，根据上下文自然填入。 2. 根据原文，社区发展出（developed）凝聚力的单位，描述形成过程，符合动词过去式语境。 3. 与'cohesive'搭配，指凝聚力的单位（units），构成社交结构的一部分，名词形式恰当。 4. 固定搭配'based on'，意为基于，这里指基于亲属关系，语法上必须用介词'on'。 5. 指亲属关系纽带（ties），是社交连接的核心，复数形式表示多个纽带。 6. 修饰社会结构，表示简单的（simple）结构，易于管理，符合上下文描述早期社会。 7. 社会结构（structure）是社交组织的框架，与'social'搭配形成完整概念。 8. 意为促进，使合作狩猎和采集成为可能，过去式动词连接前后动作，逻辑通顺。 9. 与'gathering'并列，指狩猎（hunting）活动，是获取食物的方式之一，复数结构平行。 10. 与'hunting'并列，指采集（gathering）活动，共同构成食物获取，名词形式一致。
reading.translation: 在史前时代，社会组织与主导环境条件紧密相连，后者决定早期人类群体的迁徙模式与定居选择。这些社群常基于亲属纽带发展凝聚单位，建立便于合作狩猎与采集食物的简单社会结构。领导角色自然出现，通常由拥有更优生存技能或对地形深刻知识的个体承担。资源——尤其是食物——的分配是关键因素，常决定群体内的权力动态。

reading.title: Greening: Nature's Hidden Conundrum
reading.prompt: What surprising phenomenon is discussed in paragraph 1?
reading.promptZh: 第1段讨论的令人惊讶的现象是什么？
reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Nutrient-poor regions of the ocean have long been thought to support only sparse populations of phytoplankton, the microscopic organisms that form the foundation of marine food webs. Recent satellite observations, however, have revealed unexpectedly high chlorophyll concentrations-an indicator of phytoplankton abundance-in waters traditionally considered low in nutrients. Scientists are reconsidering how biological productivity can be sustained in such environments.

Paragraph 2
One possible explanation involves a process known as upwelling, in which shifting currents can bring up nutrient-rich water from the deep to the surface, fueling short-lived phytoplankton blooms before conditions return to scarcity. Yet satellite data suggest that elevated chlorophyll levels persist over time rather than appearing in seasonal pulses, raising doubts about this explanation.

Paragraph 3
Another line of inquiry focuses on phytoplankton themselves. Some species may be adapted to survive under chronic nutrient limitations, potentially through close associations with other microorganisms that help make otherwise inaccessible nutrients available. Still, adaptation may not fully explain the broad geographic extent of these apparent increases in phytoplankton.

Paragraph 4
Finally, researchers have questioned whether the satellite data are accurate. Suspended particles unrelated to phytoplankton could distort chlorophyll measurements, complicating interpretations. If so, widely used datasets tracking ocean productivity may require reassessment, leaving the phenomenon unresolved.

B. 营养贫乏是已知背景，不是令人惊讶的新现象。

C. 正确。令人惊讶的是，传统上营养不足、本应只有稀疏浮游植物的水域，却出现了高叶绿素所指示的高丰度。

reading.translation:
第1段讨论的令人惊讶的现象是什么？

海洋中营养贫乏的区域长期以来被认为只能维持稀疏的浮游植物种群，而这些微生物构成了海洋食物网的基础。然而，近期卫星观测显示，在传统上被认为营养不足的水域中，叶绿素浓度出人意料地高——这是浮游植物丰度的一项指标。科学家正在重新思考，此类环境中的生物生产力何以能够维持。
一种可能的解释涉及上升流：变动的洋流可以把深层富营养海水带到表层，在条件回到匮乏之前催生短暂的浮游植物水华。但卫星数据表明，升高的叶绿素水平会持续存在，而不是以季节性脉冲出现，这使人对该解释产生怀疑。
另一条研究路径把焦点放在浮游植物本身。有些物种也许适应了在长期营养限制下生存，可能是通过与其他微生物紧密共生，从而把原本无法利用的营养变为可利用。不过，适应性仍可能无法充分解释这些表观浮游植物增加的广阔地理范围。
最后，研究者质疑卫星数据是否准确。与浮游植物无关的悬浮颗粒可能扭曲叶绿素测量，使解释变得复杂。若果真如此，广泛使用的海洋生产力数据集可能需要重新评估，从而使这一现象仍未得到解决。

一种可能的解释涉及上升流：变动的洋流可以把深层富营养海水带到表层，在条件回到匮乏之前催生短暂的浮游植物水华。但卫星数据表明，升高的叶绿素水平会持续存在，而不是以季节性脉冲出现，这使人对该解释产生怀疑。
另一条研究路径把焦点放在浮游植物本身。有些物种也许适应了在长期营养限制下生存，可能是通过与其他微生物紧密共生，从而把原本无法利用的营养变为可利用。不过，适应性仍可能无法充分解释这些表观浮游植物增加的广阔地理范围。
最后，研究者质疑卫星数据是否准确。与浮游植物无关的悬浮颗粒可能扭曲叶绿素测量，使解释变得复杂。若果真如此，广泛使用的海洋生产力数据集可能需要重新评估，从而使这一现象仍未得到解决。

reading.passage:
Paragraph 1
Nutrient-poor regions of the ocean have long been thought to support only sparse populations of phytoplankton, the microscopic organisms that form the foundation of marine food webs. Recent satellite observations, however, have revealed unexpectedly high chlorophyll concentrations-an indicator of phytoplankton abundance-in waters traditionally considered low in nutrients. Scientists are reconsidering how biological productivity can be sustained in such environments.

Paragraph 2
One possible explanation involves a process known as upwelling, in which shifting currents can bring up nutrient-rich water from the deep to the surface, fueling short-lived phytoplankton blooms before conditions return to scarcity. Yet satellite data suggest that elevated chlorophyll levels persist over time rather than appearing in seasonal pulses, raising doubts about this explanation.

Paragraph 3
Another line of inquiry focuses on phytoplankton themselves. Some species may be adapted to survive under chronic nutrient limitations, potentially through close associations with other microorganisms that help make otherwise inaccessible nutrients available. Still, adaptation may not fully explain the broad geographic extent of these apparent increases in phytoplankton.

Paragraph 4
Finally, researchers have questioned whether the satellite data are accurate. Suspended particles unrelated to phytoplankton could distort chlorophyll measurements, complicating interpretations. If so, widely used datasets tracking ocean productivity may require reassessment, leaving the phenomenon unresolved.

listening.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Woman: You seem out of sorts today, Aaron.
Man: I hardly slept last night. Probably just stressed over final exams.
Woman: Not really.
Man: I lie awake for hours most nights. I stopped drinking coffee after 6 p.m., but reducing caffeine hasn't helped.
Woman: You spend lots of time on smartphone apps, right? Turning things off an hour before bedtime helps me unwind. I've also started deep-breathing exercises.
Man: I do use my phone late at night, watching fitness videos mostly.
Woman: That can delay melatonin production. Melatonin's the brain hormone that helps regulate your sleep-wake cycle.
listening.transcriptZh:
请听一段对话。
女：你今天看起来不太对劲，亚伦。
男：我昨晚几乎没睡。可能只是因为期末考试压力太大。
女：其实不是。
男：大多数晚上我都会醒着躺好几个小时。我已经不在下午6点后喝咖啡了，但减少咖啡因并没有帮助。
女：你经常花很多时间使用手机应用，对吧？我会在睡前一小时关掉设备，这能帮助我放松。我还开始做深呼吸练习。

listening.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Woman: Hey, have you moved into your new dorm?
Man: Yeah, it's tiny. My clothes don't fit in the closet, and I have too many books for one shelf.
Man: I plan to get rid of a chemistry book, but I learned I need it for a course this semester.
Woman: You're reusing a textbook, didn't you finish it last year?
Man: Apparently we only use the first half.
Man: Hey, it's cheaper than buying another new textbook.
Woman: Well, have you looked into the storage room in the dorm? Everyone is assigned a large shelf for keeping things like off-season clothes.
Man: I didn't know. That might help. At least I could store my winter clothes.

Then, attendees will choose among eight virtual breakout sessions, including some focusing on the intersection between art and digital media.

So, different cultures around the world have their own sports, right? In some cases, people in many parts of the world enjoy the same sport, like maybe hockey, field hockey or ice hockey. But other sports are quite tied to the roots of a particular area. A city in England called Gloucester is known for its sizable cheese industry. And in Gloucester, um, there's a village, Brockworth. In the village of Brockworth, there's a sport that's an annual tradition involving cheese. Participants stand at the top of a hill, then someone rolls a wheel of cheese down the hill. The participants run down the hill after it, tumbling, sliding, crashing into one another on the way down. This annual cheese rolling competition has taken place at least since the early 1800s. There's no definitive explanation for why it started. Some say its origins were in barrel racing. Barrel racing? I would look more seriously at the fact that this area of England is a major cheese producer, you know? Now, maybe it's a stretch to call cheese rolling a sport. Chasing a wheel of cheese down a hill is a pretty odd activity, but if you think about it, other sports. Is it that much stranger than hitting a ball with a stick, or standing on two sticks and sliding down a mountain covered in snow? These are activities involved in sports that we consider legitimate. Maybe we're just more used to those ones though.

listening.translation: 据说话人所述，观众觉得刘易斯的陶器看起来怎样？
listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an art history class.
When I show students a small bowl by the Native American potter Lucy Lewis, they often say it feels modern, like minimalist almost. Lucy Lewis was a 20th century Native American artist, and her pottery looks contemporary, but it's anchored in traditional Native American techniques. How so? Well, Lewis learned to build clay pots from women in her community. As a kid, Lewis made pottery for tourists, sold to travelers passing through. She found ideas in publications, books, especially a local painting style that dated back to the 11th century. Of traditional black-on-white geometric designs, she saw in book illustrations, and she revived that style. Lewis painted black and white on her plates, bowls, etc. She used fine line work and balanced symmetry to interpret the old designs in a personalized way. As an adult, she became an award-winning artist, but she lived in a remote area in the southwestern United States. Due to her location, she didn't have any contact with museums or art collectors, which, I mean, honestly, sounds liberating to me. She could create designs she wanted and follow her own inspiration without interference. And these days, her pieces are sought after and valuable. Now, people sometimes assume that authenticity means keeping exactly to an old way of doing things, which can be true, but Lewis's work suggests authenticity can be procedural. You honor lineage through method, coil firing, meticulous brush control, while still negotiating new markets and new audiences, honoring your own creativity in the process.

listening.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.
Human societies can be very different from each other. Still, many researchers note that there are certain patterns found worldwide, in one way or another. These are called cultural universals. Generally, cultural universals involve basic needs, like preparing food, and inevitable human experiences, like celebrations for babies being born and rituals related to funerals. An anthropologist named George Murdock first identified cultural universals, like finding food and shelter and using language. This was in the 1940s. One that Murdock identified that I love is actually jokes. They're a worldwide strategy, a way to help people feel unified. Laughter helps ease tense situations, right? Of course, humor varies widely, but still, all societies have jokes of some kind. OK. In 2009, a team of Western researchers traveled to Cameroon, in Africa. There, they asked members of the Mafa people, an indigenous people in Cameroon, to listen to some Western music. The Mafa participants had never heard Western music before. Nevertheless, they identified the emotions that this totally foreign music was intended to convey—happiness, sadness, and fear. So, it seems that another cultural universal was discovered. Now, some theorists focus on understanding a culture based on its own standards, and what makes it unique. This is known as cultural relativism. Cultural relativism can be at odds with the idea of cultural universals. Relativism is less focused on analyzing practices across different cultures, looking for commonalities, more on the specifics of a particular culture.

content.promptText: Thank you. Can you describe a typical day for you and explain how you organize your time?

speaking.answer: A typical weekday starts around seven, when I get up, have a quick breakfast, and check my schedule. I have classes from nine until about two, and, uh, I try to use the gaps between them for reading or small assignments. After lunch I go to the library for two or three hours of focused study. Around six I have dinner and exercise a little, maybe a walk or a short workout. In the evening I review notes, reply to messages, and relax before bed at eleven. I organize everything by priority, so the hardest tasks go in the afternoon, when my mind is clear. It's not a perfect routine, but honestly it keeps me balanced and calm, even during exams.

content.promptText: Interesting. Tell me about a time when you had to manage multiple tasks or responsibilities at once. How did you handle it?

speaking.answer: Last semester was pretty hectic, because I had a part-time job, three major assignments, and a club event to organize, all in the same two weeks. At first, I tried doing everything at once, and, um, that only made me stressed. So I sat down and listed every task with its deadline. Then I ranked them, and I started with the ones that were due first. I also told my manager about my exams, and she gave me fewer shifts that week. I asked my club members to share the event work, too. It was tiring, but everything got done on time. That experience taught me that planning and asking for help are much better than panicking, and I still use that approach today.

content.promptText: Great. Some people believe that managing your time wisely can lead to higher productivity, while others think it can cause unnecessary stress and prefer a looser schedule. What is your opinion on this? Why?

speaking.answer: I'm mostly on the side of managing time wisely, but I understand the other view. When I plan my week, I get much more done, because I'm not wasting energy deciding what to do next. Uh, it also lets me enjoy free time without feeling guilty. That said, I've seen friends who schedule every single minute, and they end up miserable if anything changes. So I think the schedule shouldn't be too tight. I leave gaps for surprises and rest. I mean, nobody can be productive for ten hours straight. In my opinion, a flexible plan gives you structure without the pressure, so you get higher productivity and less stress in the long run, and that's the best of both options.

writing.answer:

Would you be willing to share your notes and let me know whether the professor announced any deadlines or changes to the project? Your notes would help me understand both the lecture and the examples discussed in class. A photo or scanned copy would be perfect if that is easiest.

A classmate

content.post: Claire: While remote work offers flexibility, it can negatively impact employees. Isolation and lack of face-to-face interaction can hinder teamwork and lead to feelings of loneliness, affecting overall job performance.

writing.answer:
I believe remote work has a mostly positive impact when companies design it deliberately rather than simply sending employees home. Paul is right that eliminating a long commute gives workers more time, reduces stress, and can improve concentration. A programmer, for instance, may complete difficult analytical work faster in a quiet home office than in a crowded workplace.

Claire is also correct that isolation can weaken teamwork. New employees especially may struggle to learn informal procedures or ask quick questions when every interaction requires a scheduled call. Companies can address this by pairing new staff with mentors, holding brief team meetings, and bringing colleagues together for projects that benefit from face-to-face discussion.

For that reason, a flexible hybrid system is strongest. Employees can work remotely when they need sustained focus, while teams meet in person for training, planning, and relationship-building. This approach preserves the productivity and well-being benefits without ignoring the social conditions that make collaboration successful.

speaking.answer: Music is really important to me, honestly. I listen to it almost every single day, whether I'm commuting, studying, or just cleaning my room. It changes my mood really quickly. If I'm stressed, some quiet piano music calms me down, and if I'm tired, an upbeat song gives me energy. Uh, I also remember certain times in my life through songs, like a summer trip with friends where we played the same playlist over and over. When I hear it now, it brings those feelings right back. So music is like a background to my memories. I can live without it, of course, but life would feel a lot emptier and much quieter. That's why I'd say it matters a great deal to me.

speaking.answer: Hmm, if I had to choose, I'd rather create music myself. I play the guitar a little, mostly easy songs I learned online, and there's a special feeling when you finally get a song right. It's not just entertainment, you know, it's like building something with your own hands. Listening is nice, but it's really passive, and I can forget a song quickly. When I play, I'm fully focused, and I forget my worries for a while. Also, creating music helps me express feelings I can't always say in words. Of course, I'd never give up listening completely, because other artists inspire me so much. But if I had to pick only one, making my own music would be more satisfying and meaningful.

content.promptText: Okay, noted. Do you think music should be a required part of children's education? Why or why not?

speaking.answer: I do think music should be a required part of children's education, at least at a basic level. Hmm, not every child needs formal lessons or an expensive instrument, but every child should have a chance to sing, keep rhythm, and hear different kinds of music. Those activities can build confidence and help students work together in a less competitive way than many academic classes. Music also gives children a way to express emotions when they aren't comfortable speaking directly. I mean, schools shouldn't force everyone to become a performer, but they should make music available to everyone. Later, they can decide whether to continue. content.post: Claire: I agree it is useful, but schools already have many required subjects, so I worry that finance lessons might take time away from academic courses.

writing.answer:
Schools should teach personal finance because students face expensive decisions after graduation. Paul is right that budgeting and saving are essential, but a course should also explain compound interest, credit scores, taxes, insurance, and the true cost of borrowing. Without that knowledge, a student can sign an unfavorable loan agreement before understanding its long-term consequences.

Claire's concern about limited class time is reasonable. Schools do not need a year-long course that displaces science or literature. They could require a short practical unit within mathematics or social studies. Students might compare two loan offers, build a monthly budget from an entry-level salary, and identify misleading claims in a credit-card advertisement.

These activities strengthen rather than weaken academic learning because they apply mathematics, reading, and critical thinking to realistic problems. Families have different levels of financial experience, so leaving the subject entirely to parents creates unequal preparation. A concise required course would give every student a safer starting point for adult life.

speaking.answer: Renewable energy matters a lot to me, honestly. I grew up in a city where the air was often hazy in winter, and I could feel it in my throat when I ran outside. Um, that experience made clean energy feel personal. I even joined a small campus club about it, and we organized a clean air day. Wind and solar power don't pollute the air the way coal does, and they won't run out. I also care about the cost, because I think cheaper clean power would help every family in the long run. I know the technology isn't perfect yet, since the sun doesn't always shine, but it's improving fast. Our city just built a big solar farm outside town. So for me it's important because it affects my health, my future, and the planet I'll live on.

content.promptText: Now, describe a time when you or someone you know tried to reduce energy use. What actions were taken, and what made it easy or difficult?

speaking.answer: My roommate and I tried to cut our electricity use last winter. Our bill was surprisingly high, so we made a few simple changes. We started unplugging chargers, turning off lights when we left, and, um, washing clothes in cold water. We also lowered the heating a little and wore sweaters at home. The easy part was the habits, because they didn't cost anything. After a few weeks, they felt automatic. The hard part was the cold evenings, when we both really wanted the room warmer. Sometimes we gave in, honestly. But our bill dropped by a noticeable amount, and that motivated us to keep going. That felt great. It showed me that small actions add up, if you stay consistent.

speaking.answer: I think the benefits of renewable energy do outweigh the drawbacks overall. Uh, cleaner air, lower dependence on fossil fuels, and more stable energy in the future all matter to me. People worry about expenses, and that's fair, but waiting usually makes environmental problems more expensive later. You know, once solar and wind systems are in place, communities can save money over time. So even though the transition is imperfect, I still believe moving toward renewable energy is the smarter choice overall.

content.post: Andrew: In my opinion, teaching communities about recycling, conservation, and environmental protection produces the most lasting improvements. When people understand how their daily choices affect air and water quality, they change their purchasing habits, support environmental policies, and teach these practices to their children, creating long-term behavioral changes across entire communities.

writing.answer:
Switching from fossil fuels to renewable energy would produce the fastest measurable environmental improvement, especially in urban air quality and carbon emissions. Kelly is right that electricity generation affects millions of people simultaneously. Retiring one heavily polluting coal plant can quickly reduce sulfur dioxide, fine particles, and greenhouse gases across an entire region.

Andrew's emphasis on education is valuable because lasting public support depends on understanding. However, education often changes behavior gradually, and people cannot choose clean transportation or electricity when the necessary infrastructure does not exist. Visible improvements are more likely when policy gives communities practical alternatives.

Governments should therefore accelerate solar and wind projects, modernize power grids, and expand reliable public transportation. Progress can be measured through power-generation data, emissions monitoring, and hospital visits related to air pollution. Environmental education should accompany these investments by explaining their benefits and encouraging conservation, but replacing major pollution sources first will deliver broader results sooner than relying mainly on individual behavior.

speaking.answer: The household task I consider most important is preparing food, because it affects everyone's health and daily schedule. In my apartment, we don't cook together every day, but we try to keep basic ingredients available, like rice, vegetables, and eggs. That makes busy evenings much easier. content.promptText: Some people believe household responsibilities should be shared equally among everyone living in a home, while others think they should depend on each person's schedule and abilities. Which view do you agree with, and why?

speaking.answer: I agree more with the second view, that it should depend on each person's schedule and abilities. Splitting everything equally sounds fair on paper, but real life isn't always equal. For example, if my roommate works late three nights a week, it wouldn't be reasonable to ask her to cook on those nights. Um, I'd happily take that job and then she could wash dishes on her free days. Also, people are naturally good at different things. Some enjoy cooking while others don't mind cleaning the bathroom. Honestly, what matters most is that everyone contributes something and communicates openly with each other. When people feel the arrangement is fair, there are fewer arguments, and the home feels more comfortable for everyone.

Fast fashion refers to the rapid production of inexpensive clothing for mass-market sales. Fast fashion allows consumers to buy trendy items at low prices and provides job opportunities in manufacturing countries. But critics argue that fast fashion leads to vast amounts of pollution in the form of discarded clothing, which harms the environment, and that workers experience poor working conditions. In your view, what would be the most effective solution to the problems associated with fast fashion?
content.post: Kelly: Based on my experience, today’s consumers demand products that are made in environmentally and socially responsible ways. As a result, market forces are effective at getting companies to adopt better practices voluntarily. Consumer demand can encourage positive change without the need for strict accountability being imposed on clothing makers.

writing.answer:
The most effective response to fast fashion is enforceable producer responsibility, supported by informed consumer demand. Andrew is right that brands should bear the cost of pollution and unsafe labor conditions created throughout their supply chains. Without rules, a company that ignores worker safety or dumps textile waste can sell more cheaply than a responsible competitor.

Kelly correctly notes that consumers can reward better practices. Buying durable clothing, repairing items, and checking where products were made sends a useful market signal. However, shoppers cannot investigate every subcontractor, and low-income consumers may have few affordable alternatives. Voluntary demand therefore cannot protect all workers or communities.

Governments should require supply-chain disclosure, factory inspections, minimum durability standards, and collection programs funded by clothing brands. Fees on excessive textile waste could finance recycling while making disposable production less profitable. Consumer choices would then reward companies that exceed the legal minimum, but environmental and labor protection would no longer depend on shoppers having perfect information.

content.promptText: Thank you. Please describe one memorable experience you have had with music. What made it special?

speaking.answer: One experience I'll never forget was my first live concert. I was sixteen, and my older sister took me to see a band I'd loved for years. Um, we stood in a huge crowd, and when the first song started, everyone began singing together. I got goosebumps. Hearing the music live was so different from listening on my headphones. I could feel the bass in my chest, and the lights moved along with the songs. What made it special was being surrounded by thousands of people who all loved the same music, and I felt connected to strangers. Afterward my sister and I sang all the way home, honestly pretty badly. I still have the ticket in my drawer, and it reminds me of that night.

content.promptText: I see. When you listen to music, do you prefer to listen by yourself or with others? Why?

speaking.answer: It depends on my mood, but I think I prefer listening alone. When I'm by myself, I can choose exactly what I want, turn it up loud, and really focus on the lyrics. Um, it's also my way of relaxing after a long day, and I don't have to talk to anyone. But listening with others has its charm too. At a party or on a road trip, music brings everyone together, and you discover new songs from your friends that you'd never find yourself. I mean, I've found some of my favorite artists that way. So both are great, but if I had to choose, I'd say alone, because music feels more personal that way, like a private conversation between me and the song.

content.promptText: Some people believe that music education should be a compulsory part of school curriculum. Do you agree or disagree with this view? Please explain your reasons.

speaking.answer: I agree, and, honestly, I wish I'd had more of it in school. Music helps children in many ways. It teaches them to listen carefully, to be patient, and to work with others, especially in a choir or band. It also helps with memory, because learning a piece means remembering notes, rhythms, and lyrics. Uh, it gives kids who don't love math or sports a chance to feel successful too. I think that's really important for confidence. Of course, not everyone will become a musician, and some students might not enjoy it at first. content.stimulusText: Your professor is teaching an art history class. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion. Make a contribution to the discussion in your own words. An effective response will contain at least 100 words. Today we'll discuss the dynamic role of art in society. Clearly, art can be a powerful form of expression and communication that can challenge societal norms and help society progress. On the other hand, some people believe that art primarily serves as a way to preserve both the history and heritage of a people, a country, or even a civilization. Which do you believe plays a larger role?
content.post: Paul: I believe that art's role in preserving heritage is its most important role. As the world becomes more globalized, different cultures are losing their identities because they have been forced to adapt to the modern world. The arts have the power to prevent languages from being lost, can preserve important cultural traditions, and remind us of what makes us unique.

writing.answer:
I believe art's role in preserving heritage is slightly more important today, although challenging social norms remains essential. Paul is right that globalization can weaken languages, crafts, music, and stories. Recordings of traditional songs or exhibitions of regional art do more than display attractive objects; they preserve knowledge and identity that may disappear when younger generations move away.

Claire correctly argues that art can also challenge accepted ideas. Protest murals, experimental theater, and digital installations can expose injustice or help audiences imagine different social arrangements. However, even this critical function often depends on cultural memory. Artists reinterpret symbols precisely because communities understand what those symbols once meant.

Preservation should not turn art into an untouchable museum object. Living traditions survive when artists adapt them to new materials and concerns. By keeping a connection to the past while allowing reinterpretation, art gives society both a shared foundation and a language for change. For that reason, preserving heritage plays the larger role.

你的教授正在上一门艺术史课程。请发帖回应教授的问题。

Dr. Gupta：今天我们将讨论艺术在社会中的动态作用。显然，艺术可以是一种强大的表达和交流形式，可以挑战社会规范并帮助社会进步。另一方面，有些人认为艺术主要作为一种方式来保存一个民族、一个国家甚至一个文明的历史和遗产。你认为哪个扮演更重要的角色？

Claire：我认为艺术可以通过呈现对传统思维的不同视角来挑战社会规范。例如，抽象艺术常常引发对既定规范和深层信念的批判性思考。通过这样做，它鼓励观众对新可能性敞开心扉，并促成改变。

Paul：我认为艺术在保护遗产方面的作用是其最重要的作用。随着世界变得更加全球化，不同文化因为被迫适应现代世界而正在失去其身份。艺术有能力防止语言消失，可以保存重要的文化传统，并提醒我们是什么让我们独一无二。

content.promptText: It's great to have you here. I'm interested in learning about your experiences with history education. First, what is one aspect of history that you find particularly interesting?

speaking.answer: One thing I find really interesting is how ordinary people lived in the past. I mean, textbooks talk a lot about kings and wars, but I'm curious about what a regular family ate, how children went to school, or what a town looked like on a normal day. Last year I read a book about daily life in ancient Rome, and, um, it was fascinating. People worried about prices, argued with neighbors, and joked in the streets, just like us. That made history feel human instead of distant. I think I enjoy this aspect because it helps me relate to people from the past. It reminds me that, despite all the changes, people have always wanted similar things, like safety, family, and a bit of fun.
speaking.translation: 很高兴你来参加。我对了解你接受历史教育的经历很感兴趣。首先，你觉得历史的哪个方面特别有趣？
